boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The header-class contrast is byte-false as a discriminator: the seeing-verb clause the row treats as distinctive to this header is byte-identical in both superscriptions, leaving only the head noun to carry the distinction; and the companion header decision states the shared fact correctly, so two accounts of the same bytes disagree inside one cluster.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, not from the challenge. The relative clause is אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה at oshb:Isa.1.1 (tokens 5-6 of 16) and אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה at oshb:Isa.2.1 (tokens 2-3 of 9); collated in both directions the run returns BYTE tier, so the seeing-verb is shared, not distinctive. The row's device_notes nevertheless read 'The header uses the seeing-verb chazah rather than the word-formula of the 2:1 header' - the 'rather than' sets the seeing-verb against the second header, which its own bytes carry. The only byte-true discriminator is the head noun: חֲזוֹן֙ at oshb:Isa.1.1 token 1 against הַדָּבָר֙ at oshb:Isa.2.1 token 1; the row's second clause ('differ in header-noun class') states this correctly, so the defect is confined to the first clause's framing. The intra-cluster contradiction is confirmed: the P01-008 device_notes say 'both retain the chazah seeing-verb and the ben-Amots patronymic', which the bytes support and which contradicts P01-001 as written. Row-internal checks that hold: oshb:Isa.1.1 is 16 tokens carrying a header noun, a relative clause and a four-king regnal list with no imperative, vocative or divine-speech frame, so the single-verse isolation ground stands; no parashah mark falls in the span and none is claimed; no ketiv/qere note falls in chapter 1 (verified against the 49-verse single-witness inventory); identity numbering, no offset zone touched, no dual owed. The challenge's ancillary observation is byte-true and independently re-derived: oshb:Isa.1.1 token 14 is יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ, the yod-initial regnal byform, returned by a token-exact skeleton sweep at exactly 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse), against 28 verses for the token-exact yod-less spelling and 30 verses for its substring form. Staged book guidance calls the yod-initial byform unattested in Isaiah; the bytes of this verse contradict that. This is a staged-guidance erratum, NOT a row defect - the row makes no spelling claim - and it carries no remedy against the row.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Field: P01-001 device_notes, first clause. Change: replace the 'seeing-verb chazah rather than the word-formula of the 2:1 header' contrast with a statement that both superscriptions carry the same relative clause (byte tier at oshb:Isa.1.1 and oshb:Isa.2.1) and that the header-noun class is the sole discriminator (חֲזוֹן֙ against הַדָּבָר֙, byte tier). Test the cure must pass: a byte collate of the relative-clause run against oshb:Isa.2.1 returns byte tier - the test that killed the original - and the corrected sentence must read consistently with the P01-008 account of the same clause. Splice both runs from source; do not re-key. No boundary change is proposed or implied.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The load-bearing ground for this cut - that the summons couplet names no offense yet - is contradicted by the bytes of the row's own first verse, and a catchword straddling its closing seam is undisclosed.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Both halves re-derive from bytes. First: oshb:Isa.1.2 is 13 tokens and closes וְהֵ֖ם פָּ֥שְׁעוּ בִֽי (tokens 11-13, byte tier) - the rebellion charge stands inside the row's own first verse. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative asserts flatly that 'verses 2-3 name no offense yet'; that is byte-false and it is the load-bearing rejection ground. The boundary_rationale's 'before any content of the charge is stated' is defensible only as a within-verse position claim about the summons (שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ, tokens 1-4, byte tier), a reading the row never states, and oshb:Isa.1.3 adds a further indictment of non-recognition, so the couplet as a whole does carry charge content. Second: בָּנִים֙ at oshb:Isa.1.2 token 8 and בָּנִ֖ים at oshb:Isa.1.4 token 9 collate at ACCENT_STRIPPED tier - a catchword in immediately adjacent verses straddling this row's own closing seam (1:3|1:4), undisclosed, and the campaign's cross-seam cohesion rule makes disclosure owed whatever the seam's fate. Object correction to the challenge, which does not disturb the finding: the challenge names the swept object as 'bare plural noun' but reports 14 verses. The bare-token object returns 8 verses (sweep: 8 verses, skeleton, token-exact); 14 is the substring object, which also collects prefixed and articled forms. The digit is right for the substring object, wrong for the object named. The challenge's rebellion-root digit verifies as stated (sweep: 18 verses, skeleton, substring). The lawsuit-vocabulary contrast the row draws outside its span also verifies at oshb:Isa.3.13. The seam itself survives on the verse-initial woe-lexeme at oshb:Isa.1.4 (byte tier), which is why the defect is a warrant defect rather than a bounds defect. Identity numbering; no mark and no ketiv/qere note in the span.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Two fields, one edit each. (1) P01-002 strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'verses 2-3 name no offense yet' with a byte-true ground - the couplet opens with the witness-summons imperatives at tokens 1-4 and the charge follows inside the same verse, so the unit is a summons-plus-indictment preface, not an offense-free preface. (2) P01-002 device_notes: add the cross-seam disclosure that the plural-noun catchword recurs at oshb:Isa.1.4 at accent_stripped tier, tier-labelled, with the swept object named (sweep: 8 verses, skeleton, token-exact). Test the cure must pass: the rewritten rejection ground must survive a byte read of oshb:Isa.1.2 tokens 11-13 - the test that killed the original - and any digit shipped with the catchword disclosure must match the object it names under a token-exact sweep, not a substring sweep. No boundary change is proposed.

boundary_proposals.grounds: The device is byte-true and independently re-derived: oshb:Isa.1.9 closes כִּסְדֹ֣ם הָיִ֔ינוּ לַעֲמֹרָ֖ה דָּמִֽינוּ (tokens 8-11, byte tier) and oshb:Isa.1.10 carries קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם (tokens 4-5) and עַ֥ם עֲמֹרָֽה (tokens 9-10), byte tier at each site. boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: A two-site, book-wide word pair carrying its two governing verbs in inverted order straddles this row's closing seam undisclosed, arguing an address running unbroken past the cut.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The lexical fact verifies exactly, digits and objects both. oshb:Isa.1.17 closes שִׁפְט֣וּ יָת֔וֹם רִ֖יבוּ אַלְמָנָֽה (tokens 7-10, byte tier) and oshb:Isa.1.23 carries יָתוֹם֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁפֹּ֔טוּ וְרִ֥יב אַלְמָנָ֖ה (tokens 10-14, byte tier): the same two nouns with their governing verbs in inverted order. Token-exact skeleton sweeps return the orphan noun at exactly 2 verses (oshb:Isa.1.17, oshb:Isa.1.23) and the widow noun at exactly 3 (those two plus oshb:Isa.47.8); across the two sites the orphan token matches at accent_stripped tier and the widow token at skeleton tier - all as the challenge states. The framing is wrong. This row's closing seam is 1:17|1:18. The second member of the pair sits at oshb:Isa.1.23 - six verses downstream, beyond the whole of the 1:18-1:20 unit and inside the span of the 1:21-1:26 decision. A recurrence that skips an intervening unit cannot argue continuity ACROSS the 1:17|1:18 seam; nothing in the bytes links oshb:Isa.1.17 to oshb:Isa.1.18. The device is a chapter-level lexical bracket, a different object from adjacent-seam cohesion, and the challenge's conclusion that it argues 'a larger bracket reaching past MT 1:17 against this cut' is not carried by the bytes it cites. Corrected finding: a genuine and notable two-verse book-wide pair goes undisclosed and is owed a chapter-level device note - and it is owed by BOTH rows, since oshb:Isa.1.23 lies inside the 1:21-1:26 span, not only by this one. It is not a cross-seam cohesion signal against this row's cut, and it does not reduce the warrant, so low. Row-internal checks that hold, and one that is exemplary: the onset שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.1.10 (byte tier) and the addressee shift is byte-carried by the two vocatives rather than inferred; the row's own recurrence handling is correct - the summons verb of oshb:Isa.1.2 matches oshb:Isa.1.10 at accent_stripped tier only, and the row explicitly refuses a byte-identical claim and labels the contrast as a byte-checkable form-class observation, which is exactly the tier discipline the campaign requires. The SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.1.17 is correctly typed, single-witness, and the only marked verse inside 1:10-1:17. Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 1.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Field: device_notes, on BOTH rows sharing the device - P01-004 (which holds oshb:Isa.1.17) and P01-006 (which holds oshb:Isa.1.23). Change: add one tier-labelled sentence naming the orphan/widow pair with its inverted verb order, per-site tiers (orphan accent_stripped, widow skeleton across the two sites), and the swept object and digits (sweep: 2 verses / 3 verses, skeleton, token-exact), explicitly classed as a chapter-level lexical bracket and NOT as cross-seam cohesion at 1:17|1:18. Test the cure must pass: the disclosure must not be phrased as evidence bearing on the 1:17|1:18 seam - the framing error that killed the original challenge - and the digit shipped must match a token-exact sweep of the object named. No boundary change is proposed.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The frame-ownership ground for this seam is carried by the English rendering alone, sits nowhere near the seam in the bytes, and recurs mid-verse inside the block immediately upstream that the row contrasts itself against; and the closing formula is called a recognized oracle-closing signature with neither tier label nor digit, that skeleton standing at 3 verses of which only 1:20 carries the ki-form.

On that object the form cannot discriminate an onset from a mid-unit interjection, so the stated rejection ground does not carry the seam, and the engagement gap is real. The four-token closing run כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר at oshb:Isa.1.20 (tokens 6-9) collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Isa.40.5, where it stands as כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר (tokens 8-11), and against oshb:Isa.58.14, where it stands as כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר (tokens 13-16); a skeleton sweep on the four-token run returns exactly those 3 verses. What holds: the onset לְכוּ נָ֛א וְנִוָּֽכְחָ֖ה is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.1.18 (tokens 1-3, byte tier) and carries the seam on its own; the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.1.20 is correctly typed, single-witness, and the only marked verse in the span; identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 1.

Tests the cure must pass: a collate of the quotative run against oshb:Isa.1.11 returns accent_stripped - the test that killed the original discriminator; and a collate of the four-token closing run against oshb:Isa.40.5 and oshb:Isa.58.14 returns byte at both - the test that killed the challenge's 'only 1:20' sub-claim, so the corrected digit must not be written as 1. boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The decision and every tier label verify exactly as written, but the one ground offered against the rival division - that the divine-speech signature at MT 1:24 is postpositive and not an onset - is contested by that form's byte position.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Re-derived from the bytes. oshb:Isa.1.24 is 12 tokens: לָכֵ֗ן at token 1, נְאֻ֤ם at token 2, and the quoted divine speech ה֚וֹי אֶנָּחֵ֣ם מִצָּרַ֔י וְאִנָּקְמָ֖ה מֵאוֹיְבָֽי running from token 8 to token 12. The signature therefore stands after nothing but a discourse connective and AHEAD of the speech it introduces: at this site it heads the speech rather than following it. Independently re-derived census: the signature stands in 23 verses (sweep: 23 verses, skeleton, token-exact and substring agreeing) and is verse-initial at exactly one, oshb:Isa.56.8; every other site sits at token 3 or later, so oshb:Isa.1.24 is the earliest position in the book bar one. The campaign's tier-disclosure law makes form-class and position labels byte-checkable claims held to the same discipline as digits, and 'postpositive ... not an onset frame in itself' is used here as a load-bearing ground for rejecting the 1:23|1:24 rival. On the bytes of this verse that ground does not hold, and it leans toward the rival that the tier-3 mark also points to. Upheld. Calibration - the row is otherwise exact and the cut is not defeated, which fixes severity at low. Independently confirmed: קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָ֑ה at oshb:Isa.1.21 (tokens 4-5) and קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָֽה at oshb:Isa.1.26 (tokens 12-13) collate at SKELETON tier in both directions and no higher, exactly matching the row's own skeleton-tier labelling and its two-verse digit; the woe lexeme at oshb:Isa.1.24 is genuinely non-initial (token 8) and governs first-person divine action, so the self-exclamation role reading holds; the PE at oshb:Isa.1.23 is correctly typed, never conflated with the chapter's SAMEKH sites, is the only marked verse inside 1:21-1:26, and is disclosed as the rival rather than buried, with confidence honestly reduced to medium_low. The challenge's 'available and unused' observation also verifies: וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה at oshb:Isa.1.25 token 1 collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Isa.1.26, whose token 1 is וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה - a byte-tier anaphora, but lying wholly on the far side of the rival cut, so it does not answer it. Not escalated: the strategy settles the precedence in play (a byte-grounded cohesion device outranks a tier-3 single-witness mark, and tier-3 never drives), and the residual 21-26 versus 21-23|24-26 question is a boundary matter the row already discloses and holds at reduced confidence - a proposal for boss adoption, not a peer policy escalation. Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 1.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Field: P01-006 device_notes (and the matching clause in strongest_rejected_alternative). Change: drop the unqualified 'postpositive ... not an onset frame in itself' at this site, or qualify it to the bytes - the signature stands at token 2 of 12, after the connective and ahead of the quoted speech, and across the 23-verse census it is verse-initial only at oshb:Isa.56.8 - and rest the rejection of the 1:23|1:24 rival on the skeleton-tier bracket alone, which the row already labels honestly. Test the cure must pass: any retained position label must survive a token-index read of oshb:Isa.1.24 placing the signature at token 2 of 12 ahead of the speech - the test that killed the original - and no digit may be shipped without naming whether its object is the token-exact signature or a substring. This is a prose and form-label repair only: the span is untouched, and re-opening the 21-26 division would be a boundary proposal requiring explicit boss adoption, never author work.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The row asserts its opening seam carries no explicit lexical frame marker; in the bytes a two-term pair that co-occurs in only two verses of this chapter sits at exactly this row's opening verse and the preceding unit's opening verse. Second and smaller: the pointed splice for the closing verse stops short of the English paired with it.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The digits verify and one object label does not. Independently re-derived: the justice noun's substring sweep returns 40 verses; the justice/righteousness co-occurrence object returns 16 verses book-wide and exactly 2 inside chapter 1, oshb:Isa.1.21 and oshb:Isa.1.27 (sweep: 16 verses / 2 verses, skeleton) - the challenge's digits are exact. Object correction: the challenge calls it 'the bare justice noun' at oshb:Isa.1.17, oshb:Isa.1.21 and oshb:Isa.1.27, but at oshb:Isa.1.27 the form is בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט (token 2), prefixed, not the bare noun מִשְׁפָּ֗ט of oshb:Isa.1.21 (token 7); the accent_stripped match at that site is a substring match, not a token match. The framing is wrong on the first point. The row asserts that the 26|27 seam is 'argued from this mode shift alone, with no explicit lexical frame MARKER'. A frame marker in this book's spine is an onset device - imperative, vocative, messenger or speech formula, superscription, header. A thematic term-pair is a cohesion device, a different object. Verified: oshb:Isa.1.27 is 5 tokens, צִיּ֖וֹן בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט תִּפָּדֶ֑ה וְשָׁבֶ֖יהָ בִּצְדָקָֽה, carrying no imperative, vocative or speech formula, so the row's assertion is byte-true as written and is not contradicted. What is genuinely defective is an undisclosed cross-seam cohesion signal - and the strongest form of it is not the one the challenge names. The immediately ADJACENT link across the row's own opening seam is the righteousness root: הַצֶּ֔דֶק at oshb:Isa.1.26 token 11 against בִּצְדָקָֽה at oshb:Isa.1.27 token 5, byte tier at each cited site, in consecutive verses, with צֶ֛דֶק at oshb:Isa.1.21 token 8 anchoring the same root at the preceding unit's opening. Adjacent-verse root cohesion across a seam the row itself grades weakest is the disclosure that is owed; the 1:21/1:27 co-occurrence is a chapter-level bracket riding behind it. Severity stays medium: the row states that it has named its sole basis for this seam, and it has not. The second point is upheld exactly as written and is independent. The row's pointed splice for the closing verse is a byte-tier PREFIX of oshb:Isa.1.31 ending at וּבָעֲר֧וּ (token 6 of 10), while the English paired with it in the same field renders the whole verse through the burning and the unquenched fire, which in the Hebrew is שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם יַחְדָּ֖ו וְאֵ֥ין מְכַבֶּֽה (tokens 7-10) and lies outside the quoted run. Quote and gloss are not cut to the same extent, and campaign law repairs that by re-cutting the gloss. What holds: the discourse-mode shift is byte-carried, since oshb:Isa.1.25 and oshb:Isa.1.26 both open with the first-person cohortative וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה and oshb:Isa.1.27 does not; the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.1.31 is correctly typed, single-witness, and the only marked verse in the span. Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 1.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Two fields. (1) P01-007 device_notes: add the cross-seam disclosure, tier-labelled and per-site, naming the adjacent-verse righteousness-root link oshb:Isa.1.26 to oshb:Isa.1.27 as the primary undisclosed cohesion signal, with the chapter-level term-pair bracket oshb:Isa.1.21 / oshb:Isa.1.27 named second and its object stated correctly (sweep: 16 verses book-wide / 2 verses in the chapter, skeleton, co-occurrence object; the site at oshb:Isa.1.27 is prefixed, not the bare noun). Leave the 'no explicit lexical frame marker' statement standing - it is byte-true and must not be edited away. (2) P01-007 boundary_rationale: re-cut the GLOSS to the extent of the pointed splice, so the English paired with the closing quote ends where the Hebrew ends. Tests the cure must pass: the disclosure must name the adjacent 1:26|1:27 pair, since a bracket claim that skips the intervening verses was what left the real signal invisible; and after the gloss re-cut, quote and gloss must cover the same token range of oshb:Isa.1.31 - the parity test that killed the original. boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The shared-feature claim across the two headers ships without tier labels, and its parts sit at three different tiers - one byte-identical, one accent-stripped-only, one skeleton-only.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Every tier re-derives exactly as the challenge states, checked in the direction the row's own sentence asserts. The row's device_notes read 'both retain the chazah seeing-verb and the ben-Amots patronymic' - one flat, untiered recurrence claim covering three elements that collate at three different tiers: the relative clause אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.1.1, tokens 5-6) against oshb:Isa.2.1 returns BYTE; the seer's name יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ (oshb:Isa.1.1, token 2) against oshb:Isa.2.1, whose token 4 is יְשַֽׁעְיָ֖הוּ, returns ACCENT_STRIPPED; the patronymic בֶן אָמ֔וֹץ (oshb:Isa.1.1, tokens 3-4) against oshb:Isa.2.1, whose tokens 5-6 are בֶּן אָמ֑וֹץ, returns SKELETON - the construct form differs in its dagesh and the name in its accent. The campaign's tier-disclosure law requires every recurrence claim to be tier-labelled at write time; this one is not, and it folds a byte-tier element together with an accent-stripped and a skeleton-tier element as though they were one grade of evidence. boundary_proposals.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, and the challenge's object choice turns out to be the careful one. Byte-true material supporting a rival the row itself names is owed disclosure in that rival's disposal, and the motif running 2:10 to 2:19/2:21 is never engaged. Calibrating force, which is why low is right: the two recurrence sites lie beyond an intervening unit, so this is not adjacent-seam cohesion and it does not bear on the 2:11|2:12 seam directly; its force is on the complex-level rival only. What holds, independently confirmed: the onset בֵּ֖ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב לְכ֥וּ וְנֵלְכָ֖ה is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.2.5 (byte tier; the verse is 6 tokens, a vocative followed by an imperative); the closing clause וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא at oshb:Isa.2.11 tokens 8-12 collates BYTE against oshb:Isa.2.17 and וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא at oshb:Isa.2.17 tokens 7-11 collates BYTE back against oshb:Isa.2.11 - the row's two-verse digit is exact in both directions; and the row's refusal of byte-identity for the loftiness clause is correct, since שָׁפֵ֔ל וְשַׁ֖ח ר֣וּם אֲנָשִׁ֑ים differs from its counterpart at oshb:Isa.2.17 in order and in the article. boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: One lens: the row treats 2:12 as a fresh unit onset without disclosing that it is grammatically continuative and lexically bonded to the refrain it treats as the prior unit's clean close. The other: the rejected alternative's load-bearing form label - an asyndetic catalogue - is contradicted by the pointed bytes, which show a waw-coordinated series.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Both items are real and they are DISTINCT defects, not one defect seen twice: the first is an undisclosed cross-seam cohesion signal at the row's OPENING, the second a false form-class label inside the rejected alternative's INTERNAL-SPLIT argument. Neither subsumes the other; they sit in different fields and fail different tests. Form label, upheld and stronger than charged. Every member of the catalogue opens with the same conjunction-plus-preposition token: וְעַל֙ at oshb:Isa.2.13 token 1 and וְעַ֖ל at its token 7, and the same token at oshb:Isa.2.14 tokens 1 and 5, oshb:Isa.2.15 tokens 1 and 5, and oshb:Isa.2.16 tokens 1 and 5 - eight coordinated members, and the governing verse coordinates its own second phrase the same way (עַ֥ל כָּל גֵּאֶ֖ה וָרָ֑ם at oshb:Isa.2.12 tokens 5-8 without the conjunction, וְעַ֖ל כָּל נִשָּׂ֥א וְשָׁפֵֽל at tokens 9-12 with it). The series is polysyndetic, the exact opposite of the label, and the label is shipped TWICE - in strongest_rejected_alternative and again in device_notes. Form-class labels carry the same discipline as digits, so this is a defect even though the conclusion it supports (enumeration inside the governing oracle) survives correction. The accompanying charge that the row calls the quantifier a preposition is right but slight: the preposition is the head and the quantifier is its object, so the two-word phrase is not simply a preposition - a wording repair inside the same edit, not a third defect. Cross-seam cohesion, upheld. oshb:Isa.2.12 opens with כִּ֣י, the same particle that opens oshb:Isa.2.6 as כִּ֣י inside the preceding row's own span, and both witnesses render it subordinating there. The humbling/lofty root chain then runs unbroken across the seam: וַיִּשַּׁ֥ח אָדָ֖ם וַיִּשְׁפַּל אִ֑ישׁ at oshb:Isa.2.9 tokens 1-4, שָׁפֵ֔ל וְשַׁ֖ח ר֣וּם אֲנָשִׁ֑ים at oshb:Isa.2.11 tokens 4-7, עַ֥ל כָּל גֵּאֶ֖ה וָרָ֑ם and וְעַ֖ל כָּל נִשָּׂ֥א וְשָׁפֵֽל at oshb:Isa.2.12, הָרָמִ֖ים וְהַנִּשָּׂאִ֑ים at oshb:Isa.2.13 tokens 5-6 and הָרָמִ֑ים / הַנִּשָּׂאֽוֹת at oshb:Isa.2.14, closing again at oshb:Isa.2.17. Independently swept, the low/bow root alone stands at 10 verses book-wide and at exactly those four sites in this chapter (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton). That is adjacent-verse cohesion straddling this row's own opening seam, undisclosed, and it leaves the strongest rival - one sustained pride-and-humbling poem with the refrain as internal punctuation - unstated. Recorded but NOT counted as a defect: the flight-from-terror motif brackets this row with no member inside its span. A device lying wholly on both sides of a row argues at complex level only; it cannot argue continuity ACROSS either of this row's own seams, so it is a chapter-level note, not a cross-seam disclosure this row owes. What holds: the opening run is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.2.12 at byte tier; the closing refrain clause is verse-final and byte-identical to the earlier site (sweep: 2 verses, byte); no parashah mark falls inside 2:12-2:17 and the SAMEKH cited at the opening seam is correctly typed - mark handling is complete and honest. Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 2. Severity: the two items differ in weight - the cohesion gap touches the onset warrant, the form label is contained to a rival's internal reasoning - and the combined grade is set by the heavier.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Two fields, two independent edits. (1) strongest_rejected_alternative and device_notes: replace the asyndetic label with the waw-coordinated (polysyndetic) description, and re-cut the quantifier wording so the preposition is named as head and the quantifier as its object; the internal-split rejection itself stands, since a coordinated series still hangs on the governing temporal clause. (2) device_notes: add the cross-seam disclosure at the opening seam - the subordinating particle shared with oshb:Isa.2.6, and the humbling/lofty root chain running oshb:Isa.2.9, oshb:Isa.2.11, oshb:Isa.2.12, oshb:Isa.2.13-14, oshb:Isa.2.17 (sweep: 10 verses book-wide, skeleton) - and state the sustained-poem rival it raises. Tests the cure must pass: the corrected form label must survive a token read of oshb:Isa.2.13 through oshb:Isa.2.16 showing the conjunction on every member - the test that killed the original; and the cohesion disclosure must be tier-labelled per site, since the chain is a root-level link, not a byte recurrence. No boundary change is proposed; adopting the sustained-poem rival would be a boss decision, never author work.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The stated ground for this row's opening seam - a fresh topical turn to the idols at 2:18 - is contested by the bytes, since the idol lexeme is already in the preceding row at 2:8 and the flight-from-terror formula of 2:10 returns inside this row at 2:19 and 2:21.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The digits verify and one of the two grounds does not survive re-derivation. Idol half, refuted on its own bytes. The lexeme stands at 8 verses book-wide and in this chapter at oshb:Isa.2.8, oshb:Isa.2.18 and oshb:Isa.2.20 (sweep: 8 verses, skeleton) - digits exact. But the challenge places the first site 'inside the preceding row', and it is not: אֱלִילִ֑ים at oshb:Isa.2.8 lies inside the 2:5-2:11 span, two rows upstream. The row immediately preceding this one is 2:12-2:17, and its bytes carry NO idol lexeme at any of its six verses. The row's own wording is scoped to exactly that adjacent unit - a fresh topical turn 'after the stanza-closing refrain of verse 17' - and against the adjacent unit the turn genuinely is fresh. The resumption the challenge sees is real but operates at complex level, and the row already concedes complex-level continuity in device_notes by disclosing the temporal tag at oshb:Isa.2.20 (בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙). This ground does not stand. Flight half, upheld, and this is the row's real defect. Two members of the motif sit INSIDE this span - מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר at oshb:Isa.2.19 tokens 6-9 and the same four-token core at oshb:Isa.2.21 tokens 6-9 - while a third sits beyond the row's opening seam at oshb:Isa.2.10 (accent_stripped tier across the three on that object; the run collates none once the majesty noun is included, since the earlier site is defective). A device with a member inside the span and a member across the seam is adjacent-seam cohesion in the strict sense, and it is undisclosed. Second and separate: the eight-token run מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ is BYTE-identical between oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 2 verses, byte), an in-span repetition of a strength the row never mentions while disclosing only the weaker temporal tag at its third verse. Corrected finding and severity: one stated ground is sound as scoped, the other is replaced by a genuine two-part disclosure gap that does not touch the bounds - so the grade drops from the charged level. What holds: the quoted opening run וְהָאֱלִילִ֖ים כָּלִ֥יל יַחֲלֹֽף is the entire verse at byte tier (oshb:Isa.2.18 is 3 tokens); the PE at oshb:Isa.2.22 is correctly typed and the only mark in the span; and the rejected alternative's negative claim is exact - the stanza-closing clause occurs at exactly 2 verses book-wide (oshb:Isa.2.11, oshb:Isa.2.17, byte tier) and at neither end of this row. The second idol site inside the span, אֱלִילֵ֣י at oshb:Isa.2.20 token 6, confirms the subject is genuinely this row's own. Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 2.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Field: P01-012 device_notes. boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The bounds hold, but the row's own stated cut criterion is met at an undisclosed in-span site - the verse-initial imperative at 3:10 - and its lexeme distinction is argued with no pointed form at all.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Both halves re-derive exactly. The in-span rival: oshb:Isa.3.10 is 8 tokens opening אִמְר֥וּ (token 1, byte tier), a 2mp imperative. Independently swept, that pointed form reaches accent_stripped tier at exactly 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses - oshb:Isa.3.10, oshb:Isa.35.4, oshb:Isa.36.4, oshb:Isa.48.20, oshb:Isa.62.11), every one an imperative address. So the defect is engagement, not accuracy: a boundary-relevant Hebrew claim carrying the weight of a not-cut decision ships with no pointed splice. What holds: כִּי֩ הִנֵּ֨ה הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.3.1 (byte tier); the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.3.12 is correctly typed and the only parashah mark inside 3:1-3:12; the PE cited at the opening seam is correctly typed; and neither of the chapter's two ketiv/qere verses falls inside this span, so nothing is owed there. boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: One lens: the row's disclosed rival addresses a unit_type labeling choice rather than a genuine competing boundary, leaving its actual strongest segmentation rival unstated. The other: this row survives every check applied to it, but its superlative carries no digit and is scoped to a work partition rather than to the text.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Both items are real and they are DISTINCT: different fields, different failure classes, and neither subsumes the other. Missing segmentation rival, upheld and the weightier of the two. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative argues trial_speech against judgment_oracle - an operative-category choice - and names no competing span at all. The identical disclosure already stands in device_notes as the mandated deviation note, so the field is duplicated onto a classification argument and the row ships with NO tested boundary rival: whether these three verses merge back into the leadership-collapse unit that precedes them, or run on to the narrative onset at oshb:Isa.3.16, is never weighed. A mandated disclosure field carrying no instance of what it exists to disclose is a genuine defect, not a stylistic one. Undigited partition-scoped superlative, upheld. The boundary_rationale calls this the clearest contend-and-judge pairing 'in this part' - a superlative with no digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit, scoped to a workflow partition rather than to a verse range or to the book, and workflow references do not belong in row prose. Re-derived independently, the bytes license a stronger and fully checkable replacement: לָרִ֖יב at oshb:Isa.3.13 token 2 stands at 3 verses token-exact (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton - oshb:Isa.3.13, oshb:Isa.34.8, oshb:Isa.58.4) and לָדִ֥ין at token 5 at exactly 1 (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton), so the pairing cannot recur anywhere else in the book - a book-scoped digit-bearing claim replacing a partition-scoped undigited one. Cross-row note: this partition-reference class recurs at P01-016, which brackets images over 'the part's own' range twice. It is a register sweep across the cluster, not two spot fixes. What holds, and it is most of the row: נִצָּ֥ב לָרִ֖יב יְהוָ֑ה וְעֹמֵ֖ד לָדִ֥ין עַמִּֽים is verse-initial and exhausts oshb:Isa.3.13 at byte tier (6 tokens); the closing signature נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת is verse-final at oshb:Isa.3.15 tokens 9-12 at byte tier with the exact title stack quoted rather than blended with the differently stacked signature earlier in the book; the ketiv/qere disclosure is exact and unusually careful - oshb:Isa.3.15 carries one note whose unpointed ketiv מלכם stands at token 1 with its pointed qere, eight tokens before the quoted signature, so the quoted run is genuinely unaffected exactly as the row says; the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.3.15 is correctly typed and the only mark in the span, and the SAMEKH at the opening seam is correctly typed too. Identity numbering. Severity is set by the heavier item: an untested mandated rival outweighs a prose-and-digit repair.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Two fields, one edit each. (1) P01-014 strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the classification argument with an actual segmentation rival and dispose it on bytes - the two live candidates are merging back into the preceding leadership-collapse unit and running on to the narrative onset at oshb:Isa.3.16 - and leave the operative-category deviation disclosure where it already correctly lives, in device_notes. (2) P01-014 boundary_rationale: drop the workflow-partition scope and re-cut the superlative to a book-scoped digit-bearing claim (contend infinitive 3 verses, judge infinitive 1 verse, the pairing unique to this verse). Tests the cure must pass: the rewritten rival must name a competing SPAN and be disposed on the row's own bytes - a field that names no span fails the same test again; the re-cut superlative must carry a digit whose object is named and must contain no workflow reference; and the two disclosures must not restate one another, since duplication is what emptied the field. No boundary change is proposed - naming a rival is not adopting it.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The row's own grammatical label for the Isa.3.18-23 catalogue is imprecise - that verse opens with a single finite verb governing an accumulating list of accusative objects, not a construct/genitive chain as the row's prose labels it - though the underlying single-unit conclusion is sound.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Re-derived from bytes and the label is a category error. oshb:Isa.3.18 is 9 tokens: בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא at tokens 1-2 (the temporal formula), יָסִ֣יר at token 3 - a single finite verb - with its subject אֲדֹנָ֗י at token 4, the direct-object marker אֵ֣ת at token 5, and then the objects beginning תִּפְאֶ֧רֶת הָעֲכָסִ֛ים וְהַשְּׁבִיסִ֖ים וְהַשַּׂהֲרֹנִֽים. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative calls the catalogue 'grammatically one long construct chain governed by' the opening clause. A construct chain is a genitive nominal sequence; what governs here is a finite verb reaching its objects through the object marker. Individual items in the list are themselves construct phrases, which is the likely source of the slip, but the catalogue as a whole is an accusative object series, not one chain. Form-class labels are byte-checkable claims held to the same discipline as digits, so the label is a defect on its own terms. Severity low is right and the challenge says so itself: the conclusion the label supports - enumeration inside one governed clause rather than an independent list-register unit - is correct, and the owner-ruled list-register finding independently reaches the same result for this very catalogue. Correcting the label strengthens the argument rather than unsettling it, since a single finite verb reaching across six verses is a tighter grammatical bond than a construct chain would be. What holds, checked in full because the other lens supported this row: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.3.16 (byte tier) and the row's role-split is right - this is the narrative onset class, not the postpositive signature class closing the preceding row. The ketiv/qere disclosure is exact: oshb:Isa.3.16 carries one note staged as a doubled token pair mid-verse, the unpointed ketiv נטוות at token 9 with its pointed qere נְטוּי֣וֹת at token 10, well after the quoted onset, so the row's statement that the onset is unaffected is true. boundary_proposals.grounds: Convergence first: the remnant item is the SAME defect independently reached by both lenses; the temporal-formula and echo items are DISTINCT additions only one lens reached. The challenge's own device-site sweep over Isa.14.1-Isa.16.12 re-derives exactly (tier-1: burden-word 2 verses, Isa.14.28 non-initial and Isa.15.1 verse-initial; postpositive signature 2 verses, Isa.14.22 and Isa.14.23; woe-family 1 non-initial verse, Isa.16.4; zero messenger-formula, zero divine-speech-verb adjacency, zero Holy-One-of-Israel title). Two limbs fail outright. The parashah limb corrects nothing: the row already reads the tier-3 setumah at Isa.14.2 as corroborating the frame that opens at Isa.14.3, which IS the correct after-the-verse orientation, single witness, SAMEKH never conflated with PE. And the challenge's own oshb:Isa.13.22 quote is EMPTY where it is labelled byte tier, so that limb ships no bytes at all.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed. (1) boundary_rationale: add one clause disclosing that the cited opening run begins with a subordinating particle whose clause is syntactically dependent on the preceding announcement, and that the seam is carried by the participant shift into Jacob and Israel rather than by the particle. (2) device_notes: add one sentence disclosing the eved-family root echo across Isa.14.2|Isa.14.3, tier named as root/skeleton level and explicitly NOT a byte-true repeated device, naming the three distinct objects (לַעֲבָדִ֖ים plural noun at oshb:Isa.14.2 against הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה abstract noun and עֻבַּד verb at oshb:Isa.14.3) so the servant referent classes are not blended into one digit. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the front-seam disclosure must name a tier-1 signal other than the particle, and every Hebrew form added must re-collate at byte tier against its own cited ref with no identity claim asserted between the three root-sharing tokens.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The bracket conclusion survives the bytes, but the run quoted as the unit's closing evidence is not verse-final, and the signature count-object is mis-specified.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Both limbs re-derive exactly from the bytes. QUOTE PARITY: oshb:Isa.14.23 has 11 tokens; the row's quoted closing run וְטֵֽאטֵאתִ֨יהָ֙ בְּמַטְאֲטֵ֣א הַשְׁמֵ֔ד is tokens 6-8 (byte tier), and the verse actually ends נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת at tokens 9-11 (byte tier). The row's word 'ending' is therefore byte-false, and the quote stops three tokens short of the very device its bracket argument rests on. COUNT-OBJECT: the couplet carries THREE signature tokens over two verses, not two -- נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת at oshb:Isa.14.22 tokens 3-5, then verse-final in that same verse נְאֻם יְהוָֽה at tokens 12-13 (bare tetragrammaton, NO hosts-title), and verse-final נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת at oshb:Isa.14.23 (all byte tier). The two verse-final stacks are skeleton-equal in their first two tokens and byte-DISTINCT (accents differ), and the hosts-title stands only at oshb:Isa.14.23, so the row's 'repeated neum-YHWH-Tsevaot signature' wording and its repeated-hosts-title signal key leave the third token and its different stack unnamed -- against the divine-name discipline that a citation names the exact stack it counts. The device is postpositive rather than an onset at both sites, so the couplet is signature-CLOSED at both ends. The tier-3 PE at Isa.14.23 is correctly typed, correctly oriented (seg after the verse) and single-witness disclosed, never a driver.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed -- the bracket conclusion survives. (1) boundary_rationale: re-splice the oshb:Isa.14.23 closing evidence so the quoted run reaches the verse end and carries נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת itself rather than stopping at וְטֵֽאטֵאתִ֨יהָ֙ בְּמַטְאֲטֵ֣א הַשְׁמֵ֔ד. (2) boundary_rationale + device_notes: replace 'The repeated neum-YHWH-Tsevaot signature' with wording that names three signature tokens over two verses and states that the hosts-title stands at two of the three, the third being the bare-tetragrammaton stack verse-final at oshb:Isa.14.22. (3) observed_substrate_signals: correct the repeated-title key so the repeated object is the signature formula, with the title stack named per site. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the re-spliced closing run must re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Isa.14.23 AND terminate at that verse's final token, and every signature digit in the row must name its exact title stack and its unit.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The mid-verse placement of the burden-word is byte-true, but the directional construal the row builds its boundary on is unsupported by the bytes and contradicted by the row's own bounds; and the row's signal key merges petuchah and setumah into one label, against the rule that the two mark types are never conflated.
boundary_proposals.grounds: FIRST LIMB UPHELD. הַמַּשָּׂ֥א הַזֶּֽה closes oshb:Isa.14.28 as tokens 6-7 of that verse's 7 (byte tier), so the non-initial placement is byte-true and the site is correctly held apart from the verse-initial header class (tier-1 sweep: 10 verse-initial header verses, unit = verses; this verse is inventoried as a non-initial site). The defect is the stated direction: the row calls the burden-word 'a backward-pointing reference to the burden it dates', and no byte supports the reversal. The same noun-plus-demonstrative construction הַמָּשָׁ֥ל הַזֶּ֛ה stands at oshb:Isa.14.4 (byte tier) immediately before the speech it introduces -- cataphoric -- and this row's own span places the dated burden AFTER the notice, so the stated construal argues for a seam the row did not draw. SECOND LIMB REFINED, NOT UPHELD: no conflation occurs. The row's prose types each mark at its own verse -- petuchah at Isa.14.27, setumah at Isa.14.32 -- and both validate against the mark inventory at tier-3, single witness, with the after-the-verse orientation correct in both cases (the PE closes Isa.14.27 so it precedes this span; the SAMEKH closes Isa.14.32 so it closes it). Nothing is read as the wrong type and nothing is counted as one object. The residue is only that ONE signal key names two mark classes in a single entry -- a field-hygiene wobble under the dotted signal-key contract, not a PE/SAMEKH conflation -- and carrying it at the same weight as the construal defect overstates it.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed. (1) boundary_rationale and device_notes: replace 'backward-pointing reference to the burden it dates' with the byte-supported reading -- a mid-verse header reference inside the regnal dating frame, pointing forward to the burden this row's own span carries -- leaving the non-initial-placement finding and the retained unit_type disclosure unchanged. (2) observed_substrate_signals: split the compound parashah key into two entries, one per mark class. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the corrected construal must be consistent with the row's own span direction and must not assert a direction the demonstrative parallel at oshb:Isa.14.4 contradicts; each parashah key must name exactly one mark class, each still validating against the inventory under the claimed type at its own MT key, single witness.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The row's confidence value exceeds the governing cap for a span that covers an entire chapter.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Upheld on arithmetic the row cannot survive. The span is Isa.15.1-Isa.15.9; chapter 15 carries exactly 9 verses in BOTH witnesses (identity numbering here -- neither offset zone touches ch 15), so the row covers the whole chapter start to finish with no remainder at either end, and its recorded confidence is 'high' while the campaign's chapter-fallback rule caps a whole-chapter span at medium_low. The cap is a live band, not a nominal one: all four bands are in use across the frozen corpus (medium_low 40 rows, low 4). Everything the challenge concedes also verifies independently: מַשָּׂ֖א מוֹאָ֑ב stands verse-initial at oshb:Isa.15.1 (byte tier) and is one of the ten verse-initial header sites (tier-1 sweep: 10 verses); the mid-verse paragraph opening immediately after the header is tier-4 layout and the row uses the folded verse text rather than inheriting a break from it; the tier-3 setumah at Isa.14.32 is correctly typed, correctly oriented and single-witness disclosed. NOT NAMED BY EITHER LENS, and it makes this more than a one-field edit: dropping to medium_low pulls the row into the low-band sidecar regime, so the cure carries mirroring and frontier-queue obligations the row does not currently satisfy. The other lens supported this row without registering the cap at all.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed -- the span itself re-derives as sound. (1) confidence: set to medium_low. (2) Because that band is now in force, mirror the row into all three sidecars with the FULL schemas (why_low_confidence, concern_type, possible_downstream_risk, suggested_reviewer, proposed_atlas_action, promotion authorities, review states), with bespoke non-boilerplate uncertainty text keyed to this span rather than to the cap rule. (3) Add the frontier-queue row the low band requires, and revisit frontier_flag_considered rather than leaving it at its drafted value. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: no span equal to a full chapter may carry a confidence above medium_low anywhere in the batch, and every row at or below medium_low must resolve to a sidecar row in each of the three sidecars plus its frontier-queue entry.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: OL: the row's own opening-seam driver sits inside an undisclosed ketiv/qere verse whose variant changes the addressee, and the span's woe-family token is left unverified. LF: the unit's own content is a plea for asylum closing on a Davidic-throne promise rather than judgment against the target nation, and this operative-category deviation from the retained label is not disclosed. DISTINCT defects, not one -- the first is a byte/disclosure failure inside the span's own evidence, the second a governance-schema omission -- and both uphold.
boundary_proposals.grounds: OL LIMB ONE UPHELD AND STRENGTHENED. Four of the five imperatives the row names as its driver stand in oshb:Isa.16.3, a variant-note verse (1 note; the campaign's largest such inventory, single witness), staged as a DOUBLED token pair at the very head of that chain: הביאו unpointed (skeleton grade only, not quotation grade) beside הָבִ֤יאִי pointed (byte tier), the two differing exactly in addressee ending. The row discloses no variant note anywhere, and it argues from that verse. Stronger than either lens stated: the addressee does not merely alternate at that one pair -- it turns THREE times inside the row's own span. שִׁלְחוּ at oshb:Isa.16.1 (byte tier) is masculine plural; oshb:Isa.16.3 sets עֲשׂ֣וּ masculine plural against feminine-singular שִׁ֧יתִי at token 6 and סַתְּרִי֙ at token 11 and תְּגַלִּֽי at token 15 (all byte tier); oshb:Isa.16.4 addresses מוֹאָ֛ב with הֱוִי (byte tier), a masculine-singular imperative; and oshb:Isa.16.5 is third-person throughout. So 'continuing the appeal's own addressee' is contradicted by the bytes the row is built on, and the undifferentiated second person of the English witness cannot show it -- the continuity reading is translation-carried. OL LIMB TWO UPHELD AT LOWER WEIGHT: הֱוִי at oshb:Isa.16.4 is skeleton-identical to the book's woe particle but byte-distinct in its pointing -- hataf-segol and hiriq against the accented holam-pointed particle ה֗וֹי at oshb:Isa.17.12 and the same form at oshb:Isa.18.1 and oshb:Isa.55.1 (byte tier) -- an imperative of the verb 'to be', not a woe onset. It is the one woe-family token verse inside this span and the inventory itself flags this site for per-site verification, so a row arguing no internal seam across exactly that span owes the disclosure; nothing about the seam moves on it. LF LIMB UPHELD AND DISTINCT: the unit's own bytes carry no header, no woe cry, no divine-speech frame and no judgment announcement -- בְּאֹ֣הֶל דָּוִ֑ד at oshb:Isa.16.5 (byte tier) closes an asylum plea on a throne promise -- so the retained massa_oracle value is an operative-category deviation, and the operative-category law requires a one-sentence deviation disclosure in device_notes that this row lacks while two comparably-postured rows in the same cluster carry theirs. Tier-3 owes nothing here: no parashah seg falls in Isa.16.1-Isa.16.5, and that absence is never counterevidence.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed. (1) device_notes: add the variant-note disclosure at Isa.16.3 -- single witness, one note, the doubled pair named with הביאו labelled skeleton grade (unpointed in the extract) and הָבִ֤יאִי labelled byte tier -- and state that the two forms differ in addressee. (2) device_notes: rewrite the continuity clause so it no longer asserts a single continuous addressee; the retained cut may instead be argued from the absence of any frame onset between Isa.16.4 and Isa.16.5, with the span's addressee turns disclosed rather than smoothed. (3) device_notes: add the one-sentence operative-category deviation disclosure for the retained unit_type, in a formulation distinct from the ones already used by the neighbouring rows. (4) device_notes: add one clause verifying the woe-family token at Isa.16.4 per site as a form of the verb 'to be' and not a woe onset, naming the pointing difference from the particle. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the variant-note sentence must validate against the note inventory under the claimed type at the MT key with single-witness disclosure; every form-class label must re-derive from the pointed bytes at its own cited ref; and no continuity claim may survive that the span's own addressee turns contradict.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The row's only mark citation is oriented backwards: the seg it calls the unit's opening stands one verse later, inside the span, at exactly the interior seam the row denies.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Upheld. The setumah is inventoried at Isa.16.6 and the seg stands AFTER that verse's words, so it marks Isa.16.6|Isa.16.7 -- interior to this row's span -- and not the row's opening seam at Isa.16.5|Isa.16.6, where the inventory records nothing at all (chapter 16 carries exactly two marks, Isa.16.6 and Isa.16.14). The error is local to this row: the same writer applies the after-the-verse reading correctly in four neighbouring rows, at Isa.14.2, Isa.14.23, Isa.14.27 and Isa.14.32. Type and disclosure are right (SAMEKH, tier-3, single witness, never conflated with PE, flagged non-driving), so the defect is the located role, not the citation. The consequence is substantive rather than cosmetic: the row's rejected alternative denies any seam between Isa.16.6 and Isa.16.12 while the seg it cites corroborates one at Isa.16.6|Isa.16.7, where לָכֵ֗ן stands verse-initial at oshb:Isa.16.7 (byte tier) after the report onset שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ גְאוֹן מוֹאָ֖ב opens oshb:Isa.16.6 (byte tier). ONE CORRECTION TO THE CHALLENGE'S WORDING, not to its finding: לָכֵ֗ן is a consequence particle binding back to what precedes, so calling it an 'onset' reads it more strongly than the same packet reads verse-initial כִּי֩ at oshb:Isa.14.1 on the front seam of another row in this cluster; the interior signal is real but it is a backward-binding discourse connector, and this tier-3 layer cannot drive a seam in either direction.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed -- the tier-3 layer is not a driver and the span is not moved on this ground. (1) device_notes and boundary_evidence_refs: restate the Isa.16.6 mark as a seg standing after Isa.16.6 (marking Isa.16.6|Isa.16.7, interior to this span) instead of as opening the unit, keeping the type, the single-witness disclosure and the non-driving flag. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the blanket denial of any seam in the span with a disclosure of the interior signal at Isa.16.6|Isa.16.7, stating that לָכֵ֗ן is a backward-binding consequence particle and that the tier-3 corroboration there is weak and non-driving. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: every parashah citation in the row must resolve to the same after-the-verse orientation the neighbouring rows use, validated against the inventory under the claimed type at the MT key; and no rejected alternative may deny a seam the row's own cited layer corroborates.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: OL: the oracle-header run that drives the row is labelled byte tier but re-collates only at NFD, and the English sentence the row calls the header's rendering is the line after the header, not the header. LF: the same header quote, the row's core seam-opening evidence, is copy-degraded and collates only at the diacritic-normalized tier. SAME defect on the tier limb (one degraded run, found independently by both lenses); the quote/gloss parity limb is OL's alone and is distinct.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Both limbs upheld on re-derivation. TIER: the row's driving run מַשָּׂ֖א דַּמָּ֑שֶׂק, cited at oshb:Isa.17.1 and self-labelled byte tier, re-collates at NFD tier ONLY -- the known degraded-quote class, canonical reordering of combining marks, curable only by a splice from source bytes. The underlying fact is sound and should survive revision: the header does stand verse-initial at oshb:Isa.17.1 as tokens 1-2 and is one of the ten verse-initial header sites (tier-1 sweep: 10 verses). The row's second run נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת re-collates at BYTE tier and does stand verse-final at oshb:Isa.17.3 (tokens 12-14), so the closing bracket is untouched and the challenge is right to confine itself to the opening driver. QUOTE/GLOSS PARITY: the staged folded verse reads “The burden of Damascus. “Behold, Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it will be a ruinous heap.” (web:Isa.17.1) -- so the sentence the row sets beside the Hebrew header as the WEB header is the oracle's FIRST LINE, and the header's own rendering is the short sentence preceding it. That is an English-side attribution the Hebrew does not carry. Fold handling verifies: the mid-verse layout fold is live at this verse (tier-4, never boundary evidence) and the row measures its English against the folded text, as it says it does. Both cited marks verify at tier-3, single witness, correctly typed as setumah and correctly oriented -- segs after Isa.16.14 and after Isa.17.3 -- so they do bracket this span.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed. (1) boundary_rationale: re-splice the header run programmatically from the source verse bytes so it re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Isa.17.1 -- the deterministic author-phase re-splice, applied class-wide to every degraded run in this batch rather than spot-fixed here, since a re-key or a copy through draft text reproduces the defect. (2) boundary_rationale: re-cut the English gloss so the sentence set beside the Hebrew header is the header's own rendering in the folded verse, and any following sentence retained is labelled as the oracle's first line rather than as the header. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the re-spliced run must return byte tier against its cited ref (the test that killed the original), and the quote/gloss pair must satisfy parity -- the English offered for a Hebrew form must be that form's rendering in the folded verse, carried in curly quotes with an inline web: ref in the same field.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: OL (medium): both pointed runs are labelled byte tier but re-collate only at NFD, and the row's own opening scene-turn run recurs BYTE-IDENTICALLY one verse past its closing seam with no disclosure, so the strongest byte-true rival goes unnamed. LF (high): the strongest rejected alternative names only generic shared subject matter when the real rival is an undisclosed lexical catchword -- the same 'glory' noun closing the preceding judgment reopening as this row's own opening image -- plus the same two degraded quotes. The tier limb is ONE defect held in common; the two cross-seam limbs are DISTINCT and sit on opposite seams.
boundary_proposals.grounds: TIER LIMB UPHELD, held in common: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא at oshb:Isa.17.4 and נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל at oshb:Isa.17.6 each re-collate at NFD tier ONLY while both are self-labelled byte tier -- the same degraded-quote class as the neighbouring header row. The substance behind them survives: the signature is verse-final at oshb:Isa.17.6 in the bytes (tokens 15-18) and its title stack genuinely differs from נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת closing oshb:Isa.17.3, so this is a second distinct bracket and not a repeated formula. BOTH CROSS-SEAM LIMBS NAME REAL UNDISCLOSED SIGNALS, one per seam, and both need their tier corrected. OL's back-seam FACT re-derives exactly: the two-word run בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא inside the row's own opening formula at oshb:Isa.17.4 is byte-identical, accent for accent, to the verse-initial run at oshb:Isa.17.7 one verse past this row's close. But the INFERENCE is mechanically backwards: the row treats that run as an ONSET marker, so a byte-identical verse-initial recurrence at Isa.17.7 marks the NEXT unit's onset and corroborates this row's close rather than arguing continuity into it. The genuine rival it raises is series-level, and neither lens reached it: the run recurs a THIRD time verse-initial at oshb:Isa.17.9, where it is byte-DISTINCT from the other two and matches them only at accent_stripped and skeleton tier. So what goes undisclosed is a three-site chapter series of which only two sites are byte-identical, and the live rival is one composite unit with internal stanzas. LF's front-seam hook is real but its tier is unstated and cannot be byte: the two tokens are כִּכְב֤וֹד at oshb:Isa.17.3 and כְּב֣וֹד at oshb:Isa.17.4 (each byte tier at its own ref), which are neither byte-equal NOR skeleton-equal -- a prefixed comparative form against the bare construct -- so the hook is lexeme-level only. LF's high severity overstates: the row's seam is independently carried by a verse-final signature with its own distinct title stack, and both cited marks verify at tier-3, single witness, correctly typed and correctly oriented (segs after Isa.17.3 and after Isa.17.6).
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed. (1) boundary_rationale: re-splice both pointed runs from the source verse bytes so each re-collates at byte tier against its cited ref, as part of the same class-wide deterministic re-splice. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the shared-subject-matter ground with the chapter's three-site scene-turn series as the mandated rival, disclosing that only the Isa.17.4 and Isa.17.7 runs are byte-identical while the Isa.17.9 run matches them only at accent_stripped and skeleton tier -- the one-sentence-plus-mandated-rival limit binds, so this rival is what goes in that field. (3) device_notes: disclose the verse-initial recurrence at Isa.17.7 explicitly and state what it argues (a fresh onset past this row's close, corroborating the cut) so the cross-seam device is on the record either way; and add the lexeme-level 'glory' hook across Isa.17.3|Isa.17.4 with its tier named as lexeme/root and explicitly NOT as byte or skeleton identity of the two tokens. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: each re-spliced run must return byte tier against its cited ref (the test that killed the original); every recurrence claim in the row must carry a tier named at write time; and no run may be called identical to another at a tier at which the two do not in fact match.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: OL (high): the row's load-bearing recurrence claim is byte-false -- the two scene-turn runs it calls identical differ in their accents -- while the run that IS byte-identical sits across the row's own front seam and goes undisclosed; all three pointed runs re-collate at NFD. LF (high): the strongest rejected alternative locates its finer-cut rival at 'the row's fourth verse', a barred positional reference that is also numerically wrong, since the renewed scene-turn sits at the span's THIRD verse; plus the same three degraded quotes. The degraded-quote limb is ONE defect found independently by both; the recurrence limb and the register/arithmetic limb are DISTINCT and each holds.
boundary_proposals.grounds: TIER LIMB UPHELD: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא and קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל at oshb:Isa.17.7 and בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא at oshb:Isa.17.9 each re-collate at NFD tier ONLY while all three are self-labelled byte tier, so the row carries no quotation-grade pointed evidence at all. RECURRENCE LIMB UPHELD: the row calls the oshb:Isa.17.9 run 'the identical opening marker' to the oshb:Isa.17.7 run. Re-collating the SOURCE runs against each other, they are byte-DISTINCT -- the oshb:Isa.17.7 run carries munach then zaqef qatan, the oshb:Isa.17.9 run qadma then geresh -- and they match only at accent_stripped and skeleton tier, with the row naming no tier at all. That is load-bearing: the row's internal no-cut argument is that the aftermath continues as one row because the same marker recurs without an intervening closing signature (and no postpositive signature does fall inside the span -- 3 signature verses across oshb:Isa.15.1-Isa.21.17, at oshb:Isa.17.3 and oshb:Isa.17.6 and oshb:Isa.19.4, unit = verses, none in this span), so an unnamed tier is carrying the granularity decision. SHARPER THAN EITHER LENS PUT IT: the byte facts run AGAINST the row's own use of them. The accent difference at oshb:Isa.17.9 is the ONLY byte-level ground on which that site could be held apart from the onset sites, and the row asserts identity exactly there, while treating as belonging to different units the two sites that ARE byte-identical accent for accent. The false identity claim therefore undercuts the decision it was offered to support. boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: LF: the row treats a mid-oracle divine-frame formula as sufficient to open a fresh row while the neighbouring row in the same part treats the same device-class occurrence as carrying no cutting force, and the row does not reconcile the two even though its own rationale names the parallel. The defect is warrant quality, not boundary falsity: MT 21:16 does carry a divine koh-amar frame, and the preceding row is plain scene description.
