boundary_proposals.grounds: Both items verify and they are DISTINCT defects at opposite ends of the same one-verse row. LF's, upheld and byte-exact: the place-phrase “בְּמָק֣וֹם נֶאֱמָ֑ן” at MT 22:23 and “בְּמָק֣וֹם נֶאֱמָ֑ן” at MT 22:25 are BYTE-IDENTICAL, cantillation included — re-collation of the 22:23 run against MT 22:25's bytes returns byte tier — and that phrase stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide, both of them here, straddling this row's own opening seam. The row's rival concedes only that 'the same figure is in view across both verses'; the verbatim device that argues continuity goes unnamed. TWO REFINEMENTS to LF's framing. First, LF cites the phrase and 'the shared root behind “וּתְקַעְתִּ֥יו” and “הַתְּקוּעָ֖ה”' but omits the stronger and simpler element: the peg NOUN itself recurs, “יָתֵ֖ד” at MT 22:23 against “הַיָּתֵ֔ד” at MT 22:25, sharing the skeleton “יתד” and standing in only 3 verses book-wide. Second, LF's root claim carries no tier and cannot be reached by a consonantal sweep at all: the mater in the passive participle breaks the contiguous skeleton, so a substring search for the root finds MT 22:23 and misses MT 22:25 — the mater-lectionis hazard class exactly. With no morphology layer in the staged extract, that root claim has to be argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, or dropped in favour of the noun and the phrase, which are machine-checkable. OL's, upheld and byte-decisive: the row's device_notes call the signature-plus-day-formula bracket 'a deliberate recurrence' of 'the pairing used at the earlier scene-shift sub-unit'. The signature “נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת” at MT 22:25 (byte tier) is the SOLE postpositive-signature site in the header-bounded valley-of-vision oracle — that census carries 23 verses book-wide and exactly ONE in this chapter — while the earlier scene-shift sub-unit opens on the day formula alone, “וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם” at MT 22:20 (byte tier), with no signature token anywhere in 22:20-24. The day formula does recur in the oracle (4 verses in this chapter), but the claimed PAIRING occurs once and has no second site, and the recurrence is asserted as deliberate with no tier label. Credits confirmed: the closing “הַמַּשָּׂ֣א” is correctly read as the common burden noun and kept apart from the verse-initial header class — the massa census lists MT 22:25 among its non-initial sites, so the row is right on the chapter's own trap; the setumah at MT 22:25 checks out and is correctly typed, though cited under a translation-side prefix rather than the MT key that inventory uses; and OL's last small point holds, the English gloss offered beside the closing splice covers a cutting-off verb that stands in the verse but not inside the spliced run.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) device_notes: disclose the cross-seam catchword — the place-phrase byte-identical at MT 22:23 and MT 22:25 (2 verses book-wide) and the peg noun shared at skeleton tier (3 verses book-wide) — as continuity evidence straddling this row's opening seam, and state the warrant that survives it; test = a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam is disclosed before the seam is claimed, and the surviving warrant does not rest on the shared phrase. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-ground the merge rival on that catchword rather than on the generic same-figure observation; test = the rival names the byte-true device that supports it, with its tier and count unit. (3) device_notes: strike or correct the deliberate-recurrence claim — the signature stands at ONE verse in this oracle and the earlier sub-unit opens on the day formula alone, so the pairing has no second site; test = the test that killed the original, namely that a recurrence claim reproduces from a sweep naming its object, its count unit and its tier. (4) device_notes: re-prefix the setumah to the Masoretic witness (oshb:Isa.22.25), and re-cut the English gloss so it covers only what the spliced Hebrew run contains; test = quote/gloss parity holds on every splice and every seg-layer claim is cited under its own witness. Any merge of this verse into the installation material is a respan PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The inclusio driver is true at the tier the row honestly names, but the bracket is built without disclosing that the same imperative cry also stands mid-span; the row's declared speech-frame key asserts a divine-name adjacency the cited verse's bytes do not carry; and the word-bound proper-name digit reports the span's length rather than the swept object's count.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Three strands, all verified, none touching the boundary. The driver is honest and I confirm it: “הֵילִ֣ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֗ישׁ” at MT 23:1 and “הֵילִ֖ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ” at MT 23:14 are NOT byte-identical but ARE identical once cantillation is removed, and the three-token cry returns exactly 2 verses book-wide at that tier — the row names accent-stripped rather than overclaiming byte, which is the tier-disclosure standard met. STRAND 1, upheld: the imperative itself also stands mid-span at MT 23:6, “הֵילִ֖ילוּ יֹ֥שְׁבֵי אִֽי”, and the exact-token sweep returns 4 verses book-wide with THREE inside this row's own span (MT 23:1, 23:6, 23:14) — and MT 23:6's token is byte-identical to MT 23:14's, while MT 23:1's differs in accent. A cry recurring mid-span weakens its own end-of-span recurrence as a closing bracket, the row offers no occurrence digit for the object it brackets with, and the refrain-keyed substrate signal rides on the undisclosed reading. STRAND 2, upheld: the row's declared key asserts a vayomer-plus-divine-name frame at MT 23:12, but “וַיֹּ֕אמֶר” stands there with no divine name in its own bytes, and the amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacency census returns ZERO verses in this chapter. The speaker is carried over from “יְהוָה֙ צִוָּ֣ה” at MT 23:11 (byte tier) — a defensible in-span inference, but not the census object the key names. STRAND 3, upheld: the word-bound check is byte-TRUE and the row is right on the homograph triple — the city name “צֹ֑ר” stands at MT 23:1, 23:5 and 23:8 inside the span, every one the two-consonant spelling, with no rock-epithet byform anywhere in this chapter and no adversary form — but the digit the row cites reports the span's length rather than the count of the swept object, which is the count-discipline rule inverted: name the object, then count it. Credits confirmed: both ketiv/qere notes in the span are disclosed at their bearing verses and both apparatus pairs re-collate at byte tier; both in-span seg sites are cited count-only and position-free; the setumah at the span's close checks out and is correctly typed. ONE ITEM NEITHER REVIEWER CHARGED: every one of those in-span disclosures — the two segs, the two apparatus notes and the closing setumah — is cited under a translation-side prefix for layers keyed to the Masoretic witness alone, while only the preceding-verse setumah uses the MT key; the disclosure layer is credited here as complete and correct without the witness flag applied to its neighbours in this same packet.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) boundary_rationale or device_notes: disclose the mid-span occurrence of the imperative at MT 23:6 with the exact-token digit and unit (4 verses book-wide, 3 inside this span) and argue why the end-of-span recurrence still closes the unit despite it; test = the test that killed the original, namely that a bracket claim survives disclosure of every in-span occurrence of the bracketing element. (2) observed_substrate_signals: correct the speech-frame key so it does not assert a divine-name adjacency the cited verse lacks — name the carried-over speaker from MT 23:11 instead; test = every substrate key is attested by the cited verse's own bytes or by the census it names. (3) device_notes: re-cut the word-bound digit to count the swept object — the city name at 3 verses inside the span, no rock-epithet and no adversary form present — rather than the span's verse count; test = the count names its object first and its unit second, and reproduces from a sweep. (4) device_notes: re-prefix the two seg citations, the two apparatus notes and the closing setumah to the Masoretic witness; test = every seg-layer and apparatus claim is cited under the witness that carries the layer.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The row's undigited universal denial of any divine-speech frame inside its span is contested by the divine-utterance authentication formula standing at its third verse — the very formula cited at 22:25 in this same range as an oracle-closing signature — and that same verse is the row's one undisclosed seg site.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The defects are real but the headline framing overstates the first one, and one digit's object is unnamed. WHAT THE BYTES SHOW. “כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶת הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה” stands at MT 24:3 at byte tier, and “כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר” closes MT 22:25 at byte tier; across the two verses the relation is SKELETON tier only, since the verb forms differ. CORRECTION TO THE FRAMING: the row's denial is not simply false. It denies a massa header, a hoy onset and a divine-speech frame, and every enumerated census returns ZERO in this chapter — no verse-initial massa header, no hoy onset, no koh-amar site, no postpositive signature, and no amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacency anywhere in ch 24. Against the frame classes the device spine enumerates, the denial holds. WHAT SURVIVES, and it is enough. (a) The denial is a universal carrying no digit-bearing sweep beside it, which is the one thing a universal in row prose must have. (b) MT 24:3 carries an undisclosed in-span divine-utterance authentication signal whose class the NEIGHBOURING row in this same cluster treats as evidence, closing that oracle on its twin — so the range applies two weights to one class with nothing reconciling them, and 24:3's possible closing function at 24:3|24:4 is never weighed. (c) The one in-span seg object, 2 segs at MT 24:3, count-only and single-witness, is undisclosed although the row engages the mark layer and the same object is disclosed at MT 22:24, 23:1, 23:13 and 23:17 elsewhere in this range — a real symmetry gap. DIGIT-OBJECT DEFECT IN THE CHALLENGE, new: the sweep is cited as '10 verses book-wide' immediately after the fuller formula is quoted, but 10 is the count for the broader divine-name-plus-utterance-verb adjacency; the quoted formula itself returns 4 verses at skeleton tier (MT 1:2, 22:25, 24:3, 25:8). The digit is right for an object the challenge does not name — the blend the count discipline bars. Credits confirmed: the remnant claim is exact and correctly class-split — the verb-family members stand at MT 24:6 (“אֱנ֖וֹשׁ”) and MT 24:12 (“נִשְׁאַ֥ר”) and at no other verse in the span, held apart from the noun, the collective noun and the personal name sharing the root — though it is carried by an unpointed mention while listed as a substrate signal, so it does not meet the pointed-splice bar that listing implies. The parashah statement is true: the inventory returns 0 petuchah and 0 setumah inside 24:1-13, and the petuchah closing the preceding unit at MT 23:18 is correctly keyed and typed. The boundary is safe on independent grounds: the other lens re-derived MT 24:3 as a candidate internal seam and found no addressee or scene shift accompanying it.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) device_notes: give the universal denial its digit-bearing sweep and name each census object — 0 verse-initial massa headers, 0 hoy onsets, 0 koh-amar sites, 0 postpositive signatures and 0 amar-plus-YHWH adjacencies in this chapter; test = every universal in the row stands beside a digit-bearing sweep that names its object and unit. (2) device_notes: disclose the authentication formula at MT 24:3 as an in-span divine-utterance signal, with its tier named (byte at its own verse; skeleton against its twin) and the sweep object named, and state why it does not close the unit at 24:3|24:4; test = the test that killed the original, namely that the same formula class is not treated as oracle-closing evidence at one verse in this range and as nothing at another without a stated ground. (3) device_notes: disclose the seg object at MT 24:3 (2 segs, single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position); test = the span-relevant seg-disclosure symmetry sweep over 24:1-13 finds nothing undisclosed. (4) device_notes: raise the remnant mention to a pointed splice from source bytes with its tier named, since it is carried as a substrate signal; test = every substrate-keyed claim is carried by a pointed splice that re-collates at the tier it names.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The row opens on a bare third-person-plural pronoun whose antecedent lies outside its span, leaving an anaphoric dependency straddling its own opening seam undisclosed; a supporting statement about the enumerated sung-praise sites is inaccurate as written; the divine-title key leaves a compound stack unnamed; and the setumah is cited under a translation-side prefix rather than the MT key.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Three strands verify; one is byte-false as charged. STRAND 1, upheld and the substantive one: MT 24:14 opens “הֵ֛מָּה”, an independent third-person-plural pronoun with no antecedent anywhere inside 24:14-15; the referent is supplied by the gleaning image closing the preceding verse, “כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת” at MT 24:13 (byte tier), which sits outside this row's span, and both witnesses read the pronoun as resumptive — the staged WEB text renders “These shall lift up their voice.” at web:Isa.24.14. The dependency is byte-true and argues continuity across this row's own opening seam, yet the rival sentence disputes only the far seam at 24:16 and the opening seam is left unargued. STRAND 2, upheld and confirmed against the controlled vocabulary itself: the row's prose states that the enumerated sung-praise sites 'begin at Isa.25.1'. They do not — the enumeration opens with a chapter-12 unit and only then reaches 25:1, so the parenthetical is false as written. It is also a register breach on its own: the sentence cites the governing strategy inside row prose, where the register purge bars strategy references outright, and the fix is to delete the apparatus rather than correct the verse number. STRAND 3, upheld: the divine-title key names the bare tetragrammaton, present twice in the span as a bare title, but MT 24:15 also carries the compound stack “שֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל” — a different count-object, unnamed. STRAND 4, REFUTED as charged: the setumah at MT 24:15 IS cited under the MT key in the row's own evidence refs, with the single-witness qualifier attached, so it is not 'cited under a translation-side prefix rather than the MT key'. The residual defect is smaller and different — the mark PROSE in device_notes carries a bare verse reference, which the convention reads as translation-side, while the evidence ref is correct; that is a prose-consistency slip, not a witness misattribution. Credits confirmed: the imperative form-class claim holds — “כַּבְּד֣וּ יְהוָ֑ה” at MT 24:15 is read as a plural imperative by both witnesses, argued the sanctioned way since the staged extract carries no morphology layer — and the operative-category deviation for applying the sung-praise label to a two-verse summons carries the one-sentence disclosure the category law requires.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) device_notes: disclose the anaphoric dependency — the bare 3mp pronoun opening MT 24:14 taking its referent from the gleaning image closing MT 24:13, outside the span — as cross-seam cohesion, and state the warrant that survives it; test = a byte-true dependency straddling the row's own opening seam is disclosed before the seam is claimed. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: extend the rival to the opening seam, not only the far seam at 24:16; test = the rival addresses the seam the disclosed cohesion actually threatens. (3) boundary_rationale: delete the strategy-citing parenthetical outright — both because the claim is false, the enumeration opening at a chapter-12 unit rather than at 25:1, and because the register bars strategy references in row prose — and carry the category deviation on the bytes alone in the device_notes disclosure; test = no row field cites the governing strategy, and every surviving claim reproduces from the row's own bytes. (4) observed_substrate_signals and device_notes: name the compound title stack at MT 24:15 as its own count-object alongside the bare title, and make the mark prose carry the same MT key the evidence ref already uses; test = each divine-name digit names which object it counts, and mark references are keyed to the Masoretic witness in prose as well as in refs.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: OL: the closing seam rests on a tier-3 single-witness mark alone — the tier-1 day-formula onset standing at the very next verse, the same onset treated as a driver at 22:20, 22:25 and 23:15 in this range, is neither quoted nor referenced, so the close is formally undriven. LF: the rejected-alternative disclosure names only the narrower 'own row for v.16' rival and omits a broader one, a recurring inhabitants-of-the-earth idiom tying 24:17-20 back to the chapter's own opening.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Both items land and they are DISTINCT — opposite ends of the row, and of opposite valence. OL's, upheld and decisive: the row's stated ground for stopping at 24:20 is a setumah at that verse, an object campaign policy bars from driving any boundary, while MT 24:21 opens “וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא” at byte tier — verse-initial, the sole day-formula site in this chapter, and the identical onset the neighbouring rows in this same range treat as a tier-1 driver at MT 22:20, 22:25 and 23:15. Neither the formula nor the verse carrying it appears anywhere in the row's prose or in its evidence refs, and the prose describes 24:17-20 as sustained imagery without saying why the sequence stops. The defect cuts in the row's favour: curing it REPLACES the barred tier-3 ground with the strongest tier-1 signal available, so the boundary is not in doubt — only its stated warrant. LF's, upheld in substance but REFINED in tier: the inhabitants idiom is real but it is not one recurrence at one tier. “יֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ” at MT 24:1 and “יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ” at MT 24:5 match at accent_stripped (skeleton “ישביה”); the plural construct “אֶ֔רֶץ” at MT 24:6 is a different form (skeleton “ארץ”); and the load-bearing link for LF's rival, “יוֹשֵׁ֥ב” at MT 24:17, is a plene singular (skeleton “יושב”) that fails skeleton identity with ALL of them — the plene-versus-defective and singular-versus-plural hazard class. The four are the only yoshev-family sites in the chapter. So the rival is a lemma-level observation, not a tier-grounded recurrence, and 'lexical tier' is not one of the four sanctioned tiers; the omission is real, the strength claimed for it is not. NEW FINDING, unengaged by the row and by BOTH lenses: a second-person-masculine-singular addressee marker stands at MT 24:17 — “עָלֶ֖יךָ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב הָאָֽרֶץ” — and both witnesses read it as address, the staged WEB text rendering “Fear, the pit, and the snare are on you who inhabit the earth.” at web:Isa.24.17, while MT 24:18-20 revert to third-person description. That address sits at the exact internal junction 24:16|24:17 where the row asserts the treachery clause 'threads without a fresh scene marker' into the terror imagery. An addressee marker is a tier-1 class under the evidence policy, and the row's continuity claim is never tested against it. Credits confirmed: the hardest trap in the span is handled right — the exclamation at MT 24:16 is correctly identified as the distinct lexeme and never blended with the woe-series onset word; the treachery run is byte-true; the mid-verse turn from reported song to personal cry is held open rather than decided; the layout fold at that verse is real and correctly denied evidentiary weight. Disclosure inside the span is otherwise complete: setumah at MT 24:20 and at MT 24:15, and the inventories return 0 seg sites, 0 ketiv/qere notes and 0 special-letter segs in 24:16-20, none of which the row claims. Medium, OL's severity, carries the row.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) boundary_rationale and boundary_evidence_refs: state the closing warrant on the tier-1 day-formula onset opening MT 24:21, quoted as a pointed splice with the verse added to the refs, and demote the setumah at MT 24:20 to what it is — tier-3 single-witness corroboration, never the ground; test = the test that killed the original, namely that no seam in the row rests on a parashah mark alone, and the same onset class is not a driver at three verses in this range and absent from the reasoning at a fourth. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: add the broader rival — that 24:17-20 resumes the chapter's opening judgment idiom rather than continuing as one voice with the 24:16 lament — with its tier named honestly as a lemma-level observation across MT 24:1, 24:5, 24:6 and 24:17 whose forms differ at every collate tier, not as a byte-true or skeleton-true recurrence; test = every recurrence offered in the row names a sanctioned tier and reproduces at it, and a rival is not credited with strength its tier does not carry. (3) boundary_rationale: test the internal continuity claim at 24:16|24:17 against the 2ms addressee marker standing at MT 24:17 — argue why the material threads on despite an address entering there, or disclose the tension; test = the row's strongest internal counterevidence is quoted and answered rather than left unstated, form class argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings. (4) Because the closing driver changes, re-derive observed_substrate_signals and confidence against the corrected warrant. The 24:16 voice-slide construal stays held at reduced confidence and is not decided here; any respan is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The decisive closing-seam ground - a person and addressee shift between Isa.25.5 and Isa.25.6 - is asserted from the English rendering with no Hebrew form quoted on either side of the seam, and the front seam is crossed undisclosed by the exalt/height root that the preceding unit's own object supplies; separately the rationale points at a governing planning document as authority for the site.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Two of the three arms hold, the third does not, and the severity is set too low. ARM 1 (upheld): the row's whole closing warrant is a person/addressee shift at the Isa.25.5 | Isa.25.6 seam, and the row's only pointed splice sits at oshb:Isa.25.1 - no Hebrew is quoted on either side of the seam it calls decisive. The claim is byte-TRUE and unengaged: second-person address runs unbroken through the span (oshb:Isa.25.2 שַׂ֤מְתָּ, oshb:Isa.25.3 יְכַבְּד֣וּךָ and יִירָאֽוּךָ, oshb:Isa.25.4 הָיִ֨יתָ, all byte tier) and closes on תַּכְנִ֑יעַ (oshb:Isa.25.5, byte tier), which the English reads “you will bring down the noise of strangers” (web:Isa.25.5), while oshb:Isa.25.6 opens וְעָשָׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת (byte tier), putting the divine name in as explicit third-person subject - “Yahweh of Armies will make all peoples a feast” (web:Isa.25.6). The engagement mandate for boundary-relevant Hebrew claims is breached at the row's own decisive edge. ARM 2 (upheld, and under-weighted by the challenge): the rationale asserts its site as 'the strategy's own enumerated first-person praise site' - a governing-document authority claim inside boundary_rationale, which the register bar forbids in row prose in every field. The challenge relegates this to a trailing sentence; it is in fact the row's most concrete and most mechanically curable defect - and the same breach class at Isa.25.10-Isa.25.12 in this cluster is carried at medium. ARM 3 (refuted as a defect, retained as an observation): the exalt/height link between אֲרֽוֹמִמְךָ֙ (oshb:Isa.25.1, byte tier) and צְבָ֥א הַמָּר֖וֹם בַּמָּר֑וֹם (oshb:Isa.24.21, byte tier) is NOT byte-true and not even a contiguous consonantal match - swept per attested spelling the mem-prefixed spelling stands at 13 verses book-wide and 4 in chs 23-27 (sweep: 4 verses - oshb:Isa.24.4, oshb:Isa.24.18, oshb:Isa.24.21, oshb:Isa.26.5) and the bare spelling at 7 book-wide and 2 here (sweep: 2 verses - oshb:Isa.23.4, oshb:Isa.25.1); the challenge's own digits verify exactly. The cross-seam cohesion rule binds byte-true devices straddling a row's own seam; a root-level echo at two different spellings is a disclosure courtesy, not a rule breach, and cannot carry severity on its own. Mark layer is correct as both primaries say: PE after oshb:Isa.24.23 and PE after oshb:Isa.25.5 bracket the span exactly, types unconflated, single-witness disclosed, and no mark falls inside Isa.25.1-Isa.25.5 (tier-3, absence not used either way).
boundary_proposals.remedy: boundary_rationale: (a) delete the clause 'the strategy's own enumerated first-person praise site' outright - the site must be argued from this row's own bytes and nothing else; (b) add pointed splices on BOTH sides of the closing seam - תַּכְנִ֑יעַ (oshb:Isa.25.5, byte tier) and וְעָשָׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת (oshb:Isa.25.6, byte tier) - with the form-class label held as a byte-checkable claim, since no morphology layer is available. Optional in device_notes: one sentence disclosing the exalt/height echo to oshb:Isa.24.21 as root-level per attested spelling, explicitly NOT byte-identical. No boundary change is proposed and none is needed. TESTS the cure must pass: the register scan finds no governing-document or planning-file reference in any field; every Hebrew run in the row re-collates at byte tier against its cited verse; the closing-seam sentence names a tier for every form it labels.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The row makes a demonstrative mountain-phrase its identifying frame without disclosing that the same phrase recurs on the far side of its own closing seam and without naming the tier at which the far site matches; and the divine-name object at Isa.25.8 goes unnamed while only the hosts-title is engaged.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The tier finding is exactly right and is the real defect; the 'runs through' framing and the divine-name arm are not. VERIFIED: בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה stands byte-identical at oshb:Isa.25.6 and oshb:Isa.25.7 (sweep: 2 verses at byte tier) and recurs at oshb:Isa.25.10 as בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה - the accents differ, so the third site matches only at accent_stripped / skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses at those tiers, 2 at byte). The row makes the phrase its identifying frame ('matching בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Isa.25.6, byte tier)') and discloses neither the in-span repetition at oshb:Isa.25.7 nor the recurrence past its own closing edge nor the tier drop at that far site - and the campaign standard requires the tier named on EVERY recurrence claim. CORRECTION to the framing: the phrase does not 'run oshb:Isa.25.6 through oshb:Isa.25.10'. oshb:Isa.25.8 and oshb:Isa.25.9 carry no occurrence at any tier, so the signal is three sites with a two-verse gap, and no site sits on either side of the row's own 25:8 | 25:9 seam. It argues a mountain-motif band reaching two verses past the row's close, which is a real disclosure obligation, but it is weaker than a device straddling the seam itself. REFUTED arm: אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה does stand byte-true at oshb:Isa.25.8, but the row makes no divine-name count claim anywhere - it names a title as span texture - and the count-object discipline bites on digits and swept objects, not on an obligation to enumerate every title present in a span. This is an observation, not a defect. That is a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam and it is answered nowhere. NEW FINDING (cross-check): the LF packet verified this same fold as 'confirmed against the staged verse map' and accepted the row's description - the existence digit was reproduced with the wrong count-object, which is the defect class the peer round exists to catch. Correct as written in the row: the opening splice properly includes the governing particle כִּֽי תָנ֥וּחַ; the ketiv/qere note at oshb:Isa.25.10 is disclosed single-witness and the quotation stops well before the staged doubled pair; SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.25.12 matches the inventory under the right type.

Its closing edge is carried entirely by where the translation's closing quotation mark falls at web:Isa.26.6, plus the absence of further quotation punctuation before web:Isa.27.2, and strongest_rejected_alternative repeats that same punctuation ground and nothing else. The row therefore has NO admissible warrant for its back edge, and the co-primary packet supported this row while itself labelling the driver tier-4 - an internal inconsistency that does not survive the bytes. Hebrew grounds for the same seam exist unused, exactly as the challenge says: oshb:Isa.26.7 opens אֹ֥רַח לַצַּדִּ֖יק מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים (byte tier) on a fresh gnomic subject. Unquoted-form gaps verified: the imperative at 26:4 stands in the bytes as בִּטְח֥וּ (oshb:Isa.26.4, byte tier) and is quoted only in English; the short-form divine title stands as בְּיָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.26.4, byte tier), and although the row's digit is right (the short form is one of exactly three book-wide sites - oshb:Isa.12.2, oshb:Isa.26.4, oshb:Isa.38.11), a form-class label and a divine-title object are byte-checkable claims and owe the bytes, not the rendering. Front seam undisclosed, verified: עַד עָפָֽר is byte-identical at exactly oshb:Isa.25.12 and oshb:Isa.26.5 (sweep: 2 verses book-wide), one site immediately outside this row and one inside it. Back-seam catchword verified too: the righteous-one term stands at oshb:Isa.26.2 and twice at oshb:Isa.26.7, and its lamed-prefixed spelling at exactly two verses book-wide at skeleton tier (sweep: 2 verses - oshb:Isa.24.16, oshb:Isa.26.7). Correct as written: SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.25.12 is cited under the right type, and the inventory records no parashah mark inside Isa.26.1-Isa.26.6, as the row claims (tier-3, single-witness, absence not used as counterevidence).

Add the seam-pair front-edge disclosure of the עַד עָפָֽר bracket (byte tier, sweep: 2 verses book-wide) as ONE edit shared with the preceding row. No boundary change is proposed: the span may well be right, but its warrant must be re-cut. boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: LF: the row quotes web:Isa.26.20 as its own close-boundary evidence without disclosing that the underlying Masoretic verse is ketiv/qere-bearing. OL: the stated reason for rejecting the internal marks is byte-false at the first of them, the row's own closing criterion is already satisfied inside its last verse, and it quotes the doubled ketiv/qere verse at its back seam with no ketiv/qere disclosure anywhere in the row.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The two packets OVERLAP on one arm (the undisclosed ketiv/qere) and OL adds two arms the other packet did not reach. All three are real. ARM 1, OL only, and the reason the severity is high: strongest_rejected_alternative rejects both internal marks on the ground that 'neither break carries an addressee or person shift' and that the second-person appeal 'persists in the same voice from Isa.26.7 through Isa.26.19'. The bytes contradict that at the first mark. The 2ms pronominal-suffix grapheme occurs twice in oshb:Isa.26.9, ZERO times in oshb:Isa.26.10, and twice in oshb:Isa.26.11 (count: 2 / 0 / 2, graphemic, over the pointed bytes); oshb:Isa.26.10 closes on גֵּא֥וּת יְהוָֽה - “will not see Yahweh’s majesty.” (web:Isa.26.10) - a third-person reference to the divine name, and oshb:Isa.26.11 opens verse-initially יְהוָ֛ה רָ֥מָה יָדְךָ֖ (byte tier), resuming direct address. The SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.26.10 therefore sits exactly where second-person address resumes - the one place in the span where the row's own stated criterion is met - so a tier-3 mark is overridden on a ground that is false at that mark. The row's blanket claim is nevertheless TRUE at the second mark: 2ms address stands on both sides of the break after oshb:Isa.26.11 (oshb:Isa.26.12 פָּעַ֥לְתָּ, oshb:Isa.26.13 זֽוּלָתֶ֑ךָ and בְּךָ֖, byte tier), and the challenge correctly scoped its finding to 'the first one'. Note the marks stay tier-3 weak and cannot drive an edge in either direction; the defect is the false reason, not the decision. ARM 2, OL only, correctly HELD rather than asserted: the closing criterion (a voice commanding the community, said to begin only at 26:20) is already present inside the row's final verse - הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר (oshb:Isa.26.19, byte tier; the two runs are each unique in the book, sweep: 1 verse each), rendered “Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust” (web:Isa.26.19). With no morphology layer staged this is a form-class reading, and the challenge flags it as held; the point stands as stated - the criterion as written does not separate 26:19 from 26:20. ARM 3, BOTH packets, same defect: the row quotes “Come, my people, enter into your rooms” (web:Isa.26.20) as its close-boundary evidence with no ketiv/qere disclosure anywhere, while oshb:Isa.26.20 carries TWO notes staged as the doubled pairs דלתיך דְּלָתְךָ֖ and יעבור יַעֲבָר (single-witness); the adjacent row quoting the same verse does disclose both. The machine arm agrees - the citation sweep raises a ketiv/qere-versus-WEB-quote warning on this row and on no other row in the assignment. NEW FINDING neither packet reached: the variant is LOAD-BEARING for the quoted evidence, not merely adjacent to it. The English clause the row leans on renders “shut your doors behind you” (web:Isa.26.20) in the plural, aligning with the ketiv spelling דלתיך against the qere דְּלָתְךָ֖, and “until the indignation is past” (web:Isa.26.20) sits on the second note; held as a rendering-alignment observation, since no morphology layer is staged. Correct as written: אֹ֥רַח לַצַּדִּ֖יק מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים and the resurrection splice both re-collate at byte tier in their cited verses, and the SAMEKH marks after oshb:Isa.26.10, oshb:Isa.26.11 and oshb:Isa.26.19 are all disclosed under the right type as single-witness.
boundary_proposals.remedy: (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: rewrite so the stated ground is byte-true. It must concede the person shift at the break after oshb:Isa.26.10 - splice גֵּא֥וּת יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.26.10) and יְהוָ֛ה רָ֥מָה יָדְךָ֖ (oshb:Isa.26.11), both byte tier - and then argue the unit holds across it on some other tier-1 ground, or record the rival and re-check the confidence band; the blanket 'neither break carries an addressee or person shift' sentence cannot survive. Keep the marks explicitly tier-3 weak and non-driving. (2) boundary_rationale: re-cut the closing criterion so it distinguishes oshb:Isa.26.19 from oshb:Isa.26.20 - splice הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר (oshb:Isa.26.19, byte tier), name the form-class as a byte-checkable claim, and state what separates the two verses beyond 'a voice commanding the community'. (3) SEAM-PAIR EDIT with the following row, one edit: add the ketiv/qere disclosure for oshb:Isa.26.20 (two notes, single-witness, quotation stopping before both staged pairs) AND note that the English clause quoted renders the plural, aligning with the ketiv - or stop quoting that clause. No boundary change proposed. TESTS: the citation sweep's ketiv/qere-versus-WEB-quote warning no longer fires on this row; a 2ms-suffix grapheme count over oshb:Isa.26.9 / 26.10 / 26.11 returns 2 / 0 / 2 and the rewritten sentence agrees with it; every form-class label in the row is held or byte-shown; the same ketiv/qere disclosure appears on both sides of the seam pair.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The closing-seam ground names a frame formula in the next verse without ever quoting it, and the root repetition that hooks Isa.26.21 straight into Isa.27.1 across that seam is undisclosed; the front-edge criterion is also already present one verse earlier.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The engagement arm is upheld; the 'nowhere answered' framing of the cohesion arm is overstated and the tier is not what the wording implies. REFINED, cohesion arm: the hook is real but weaker and differently tiered than stated. This row's closing word is לִפְקֹ֛ד (oshb:Isa.26.21, byte tier, unique in the book at sweep: 1 verse) and the next verse continues יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier); the two forms are NOT byte-identical to each other - they share the consonantal skeleton only, which stands at 18 verses book-wide (sweep: 18 verses), while the fuller construction the challenge cites stands at exactly 3 verses at accent_stripped / skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses - oshb:Isa.23.17, oshb:Isa.24.21, oshb:Isa.27.1), reopening the frame that opened this cluster at יִפְקֹ֧ד יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.24.21, byte tier). And the row does not leave the continuity wholly unanswered: its rationale states in terms that the verse 'continues without a further addressee change into the leviathan judgment of Isa.27.1' and rests the cut on the fresh formula plus the mark layer. What is missing is the Hebrew-level catchword and its tier, not the acknowledgement. The challenge's front-edge point verifies and is correctly held as a form-class reading: הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר (oshb:Isa.26.19, byte tier) already reverses the direction of address one verse before the row opens, so the row's distinguishing criterion does not by itself separate the two verses. Correct as written and worth recording: the ketiv/qere handling here is exact - the splice stops at וּֽסְגֹ֥ר, before both staged pairs, with the doubling disclosed single-witness; SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.26.19 and after oshb:Isa.26.21 are cited under the right type.
boundary_proposals.remedy: boundary_rationale: splice the following verse's onset בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier) into the closing-seam sentence and add oshb:Isa.27.1 to boundary_evidence_refs, so the seam driver is engaged in the bytes on both sides. device_notes: add one sentence disclosing the visitation catchword across the seam - לִפְקֹ֛ד (oshb:Isa.26.21) and יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.1), each byte tier in its own verse, linked at consonantal skeleton only (sweep: 18 verses book-wide on that skeleton) - and say why it does not bind the two units into one.
