boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The one-verse unit's onset and both its mark disclosures are byte-true, but a divine-visitation catchword runs across both of its seams undisclosed, and the onset formula it leans on is a large class carried without a digit.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Both arms point at something real; the first names the wrong count-object and the second reaches past this row's own burden. ARM 1, REFINED - the object is blended. The three sites verify in the bytes: לִפְקֹ֛ד (oshb:Isa.26.21), יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.1) and פֶּ֚ן יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.3), all byte tier in their cited verses, with the root skeleton at 18 verses book-wide (sweep: 18 verses) exactly as the challenge says. But calling all three 'a divine-visitation chain' blends two speech-roles into one swept object, which the count-discipline bars: at oshb:Isa.26.21 and oshb:Isa.27.1 the visiting agent is the divine name itself, while oshb:Isa.27.3 is a negative-purpose clause inside first-person divine speech in which the speaker is the vineyard's KEEPER and the visiting agent is someone else - “Lest anyone damage it” (web:Isa.27.3). CORRECTED FINDING, and it is sharper than the original at the back edge: יִפְקֹ֣ד is BYTE-identical at exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses - oshb:Isa.27.1 and oshb:Isa.27.3), so a byte-true lexical recurrence does cross this row's closing edge and is undisclosed - but it must be cited as that lexical form, not as a visitation chain. At the front edge the link to לִפְקֹ֛ד is skeleton-level only, not byte. The 'straddling BOTH edges' wording also skips that oshb:Isa.27.2 carries no occurrence at any tier. ARM 2, part UPHELD, part out of scope. Upheld: the row's sole onset driver is the day formula and it carries no digit and no swept object anywhere in the row, although the class is large and unevenly distributed across tiers - the byte-tier form the row quotes, בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא, stands at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses at byte tier - oshb:Isa.7.20, oshb:Isa.19.18, oshb:Isa.27.1), while the same formula at skeleton tier stands at 45 verses book-wide (sweep: 45 verses), and the challenge's 45-verse digit is correct for that object. The formula is also not a member of the staged tier-1 frame spine, so its discriminating power is exactly the thing the row leaves unquantified - and the very next verse opens the same formula at accent_stripped tier (בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא, oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier in its own verse; the two openers differ in their accents, so they are NOT byte-identical to each other), which is the row's own seam. Out of scope: 'does not distinguish the bare form from the waw-prefixed long form used two rows later' compares this row against other rows' choices; that is a cross-row consistency question for the campaign, not a defect in this row's prose, and stating it positionally is itself barred register. Correct as the challenge concedes: every Hebrew run in the row matches its cited verse at byte tier, and SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.26.21 and after oshb:Isa.27.1 are correctly typed, correctly keyed to the Hebrew witness, and disclosed single-witness and non-driving (tier-3).
boundary_proposals.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: give the onset formula a swept object and a digit at the tier quoted - the byte-tier form at 3 verses book-wide, or the formula class at skeleton tier at 45 verses book-wide, naming which - and state what distinguishes this onset from the identical bare formula opening the very next verse, since both cannot be onsets on the formula alone. (2) device_notes: add one sentence disclosing the byte-identical recurrence of יִפְקֹ֣ד at oshb:Isa.27.1 and oshb:Isa.27.3 (byte tier, sweep: 2 verses book-wide) across this row's closing edge, naming the lexical form as the object and noting that the two sites carry different speech-roles; the front-edge link to לִפְקֹ֛ד may be added as skeleton-level only, explicitly NOT byte. Do NOT write it up as a divine-visitation chain. No boundary change proposed. TESTS: every recurrence and class claim in the row carries a tier AND a digit with its unit named; a byte-tier sweep of the cited visitation form returns exactly oshb:Isa.27.1 and oshb:Isa.27.3; the universals check finds no undigited class claim; no field carries a positional cross-row reference.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The song-frame identification at the onset verse and the close at 27:5 both rest on English rendering choices that the Hebrew of the cited verses does not carry; and the quote/gloss pairing inverts the Hebrew word order.
boundary_proposals.grounds: All three arms verify, and the challenge is if anything too generous on the third. ARM 1: the onset verse carries no song lexeme at any tier. oshb:Isa.27.2 reads בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (byte tier) - six tokens, none of them the song noun or its cognate verb, which stand together at יוּשַׁ֥ר הַשִּׁיר (oshb:Isa.26.1, byte tier, unique in the book at sweep: 1 verse) and whose consonantal skeleton stands at 9 verses book-wide (sweep: 9 verses), the nearest being oshb:Isa.26.1 itself. The row nevertheless calls this 'a second, separate song frame' and its signal keys carry a song-announcement formula, so a frame class with a real instance one chapter earlier is imported into a verse whose bytes carry no such form. The construal of עַנּוּ לָֽהּ as an order to sing is defensible on its own, and the unit_type is not what is being challenged - the defect is a FORMULA claim asserted without the form present in the cited verse. ARM 2, the sharpest and most mechanically curable: the quote/gloss pairing inverts the Hebrew. The row pairs the English clause “In that day, sing to her,” (web:Isa.27.2) with the whole six-token run and then presents “A pleasant vineyard!” (web:Isa.27.2) as a quotation INTRODUCED by that run - but כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier), the words so rendered, are the THIRD and FOURTH tokens inside the very run cited, standing before the verb. The 'formula, then introduced quotation' sequencing exists only because the English reorders the clause; the full English is “In that day, sing to her, “A pleasant vineyard!” (web:Isa.27.2). Quote/gloss parity is campaign law and the gloss must be re-cut. ARM 3: the close's first arm is where the English quotation mark falls - “Let him make peace with me.” (web:Isa.27.5) - and the pointed bytes of oshb:Isa.27.2 through oshb:Isa.27.5 carry letters and accents and no quotation delimitation at any tier, so that arm is a tier-4 rendering artifact and can never set an edge; the material inside the English quotation is itself first-person divine speech, which the delimiter does not track. ADDED, and it strengthens rather than softens the challenge: the second, byte-grounded arm of the close does NOT survive as stated either. The row argues a new opening at 27:6 from the English “In days to come, Jacob will take root” (web:Isa.27.6) and quotes no Hebrew there at all. The bytes give הַבָּאִים֙ (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier), a bare participial form unique in the book (sweep: 1 verse) and not a member of the staged tier-1 frame spine; the noun that makes it read as a dated formula is supplied by the translation. So both halves of this row's closing warrant are carried by the rendering. Correct as written: the two Hebrew runs the row does quote reach byte tier in their cited verses, the SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.27.1 is cited under the right type as single-witness, the inventory records no further mark inside Isa.27.2-Isa.27.5 as the row says, and the cross-part vineyard relation to Isa.5.1-Isa.5.7 is properly quarantined as typed metadata.
boundary_proposals.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: re-cut the gloss so quote and Hebrew agree - either splice the onset's two tokens alone and gloss כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד separately in its own place in the run, or quote the whole run against the whole English clause “In that day, sing to her, “A pleasant vineyard!” (web:Isa.27.2); the introduced-quotation sequencing must go. (2) Replace the song-FRAME assertion with what the bytes support: an onset formula plus a construal of עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier), stated as a construal, with the song-announcement signal key dropped or re-keyed, since the formula's real instance is at oshb:Isa.26.1 and not here. (3) Re-warrant the closing edge from bytes: splice הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier), add oshb:Isa.27.6 to boundary_evidence_refs, and say what the form is (a bare participial onset, not a staged frame class); the English quotation mark may remain only as an explicitly tier-4, non-driving corroboration. No boundary change is proposed. TESTS: no field rests an edge on translation punctuation or on a noun the translation supplies; every English gloss maps to the Hebrew tokens actually inside the run it is paired with; every formula/frame claim names a form present in the cited verse's own bytes with its tier.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The row's load-bearing reason for overriding a marked internal break is a plural English pronoun that does not stand in either of the two verses it is claimed for, and a feminine-suffix chain reaching back across the row's own front seam is undisclosed; the onset is also called a fresh formula though it is a bare participial form.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Two arms hold; the suffix-chain arm is byte-false as framed. ARM 1 UPHELD, and it is the load-bearing one: strongest_rejected_alternative sets aside a single-witness setumah recorded after MT 27:6 on the ground that 'the pronoun "them" opening Isa.27.7 has no antecedent besides Jacob and Israel named in Isa.27.6'. No such pronoun stands there. oshb:Isa.27.7 opens הַכְּמַכַּ֥ת (byte tier), an interrogative-comparative construction, and its suffixes are third masculine singular - מַכֵּ֖הוּ הִכָּ֑הוּ and הֲרֻגָ֖יו (byte tier) - while the English “Has he struck them as he struck those who struck them?” (web:Isa.27.7) renders them collectively and does not put 'them' at the head of the verse either. The referential conclusion may still be reachable from those 3ms forms, but the row quotes no Hebrew from 27:7-8 at all and never makes that argument, so a tier-3 mark is overridden on a ground available only in the rendering. ADDED PRECISION: the row's rationale extends one English 'them' across 'Isa.27.7-8', but the suffixes at oshb:Isa.27.8 are third feminine singular - בְּשַׁלְחָ֣הּ תְּרִיבֶ֑נָּה (byte tier) - so a single pronoun is being carried over TWO different suffix classes. Held as a form-class reading, since no morphology layer is staged. ARM 2 REFUTED AS FRAMED: there is no 3fs chain 'straddling the 27:5 | 27:6 seam'. The feminine suffixes run oshb:Isa.27.2 (עַנּוּ לָֽהּ), oshb:Isa.27.3 (נֹֽצְרָ֔הּ לִרְגָעִ֖ים אַשְׁקֶ֑נָּה) and oshb:Isa.27.4 (אֶפְשְׂעָ֥ה בָ֖הּ אֲצִיתֶ֥נָּה), all byte tier - and then STOP: oshb:Isa.27.5 carries first-person forms instead (יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה שָׁל֖וֹם לִ֑י, byte tier), oshb:Isa.27.6 carries no pronominal suffix at all, and oshb:Isa.27.7 is 3ms. They resume only at oshb:Isa.27.8, two verses past the seam. The real observation - a feminine object reappearing at 27:8 that may reach back to the vineyard - is worth disclosing, but it does not cross this row's front edge as a chain and cannot argue continuity there. ARM 3 UPHELD: הַבָּאִים֙ (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier) is unique in the book (sweep: 1 verse) and is a bare participial form, not a member of the staged tier-1 frame spine; calling it 'a fresh formula' while quoting the English “In days to come, Jacob will take root” (web:Isa.27.6), which supplies the noun, labels a class the bytes do not carry. Correct as the challenge concedes: the two Hebrew runs the row quotes reach byte tier, and the SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.27.6 and after oshb:Isa.27.11 are correctly typed and correctly keyed to the Hebrew witness. The row is already held at reduced confidence with its frontier flag set, which is the right posture for this stretch.
boundary_proposals.remedy: (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: rewrite the override on Hebrew ground or drop it. It must splice מַכֵּ֖הוּ הִכָּ֑הוּ (oshb:Isa.27.7, byte tier) and name the suffix class as a byte-checkable, held form-class claim, and it must stop attributing one plural pronoun to 27:7 and 27:8 together, since בְּשַׁלְחָ֣הּ תְּרִיבֶ֑נָּה (oshb:Isa.27.8, byte tier) is a different class; add oshb:Isa.27.7 and oshb:Isa.27.8 to boundary_evidence_refs. Keep the mark tier-3 weak and non-driving either way. (2) boundary_rationale: replace 'a fresh formula' with what the bytes give - splice הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier) and describe it as a bare participial onset, noting that the dating noun is supplied by the rendering. (3) Do NOT add a feminine-suffix 'chain across the front seam' - if the 27:8 feminine object is disclosed at all, it must be cited as a resumption after oshb:Isa.27.5-27.7 carry none. No boundary change proposed. TESTS: every pronoun/suffix claim in the row names a verse, a form, and a tier, and is held where no morphology layer supports it; no claim describes a suffix class that a sweep of the cited verse's bytes contradicts; the reference mirror shows every verse argued in prose present in boundary_evidence_refs.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The split of the two adjacent day-formula verses is defended by a generalized pattern claim with no digit and by importing a different device class, while the linking form shared by both onsets is never weighed; the long form stands in 13 verses book-wide and these two are its only adjacent pair.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The disclosure residue is real but small, and two of the challenge's own load-bearing claims are byte-false. BYTE-FALSE 1 - the exclusivity claim: the waw-prefixed long onset stands at 13 verses book-wide at skeleton tier (sweep: 13 verses - oshb:Isa.7.18, 7.21, 7.23, 10.20, 10.27, 11.10, 11.11, 17.4, 22.20, 23.15, 24.21, 27.12, 27.13), and that set contains TWO adjacent pairs, not one: oshb:Isa.11.10 | oshb:Isa.11.11 as well as oshb:Isa.27.12 | oshb:Isa.27.13. 'These two are its only adjacent pair' does not survive the sweep it cites. BYTE-FALSE 2 - the identity claim: the two onsets are NOT the identical form at byte tier. וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.27.12) and וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.27.13) each re-collate at byte tier in their own verse but differ from each other in their accents; they agree only at accent_stripped and skeleton tier. Calling them 'identical' is exactly the accent-blind framing the tier-disclosure standard exists to prevent. WHAT SURVIVES, and it is a low-grade disclosure gap rather than a warrant failure: the row carries no digit and no tier for the onset formula it makes its splitting ground, and the bare form it treats as a unit onset two rows earlier is a much larger object (sweep: 45 verses at skeleton tier) than the long form here, so two distinct spellings do sit under one undifferentiated signal key. REFINED on the massa arm: the header class IS a different object - exactly 10 verse-initial sites, bounding parent oracles, none of them in this chapter - so the analogy borrows warrant from a class the row is not using. But this is an appeal to analogy, not a blended sweep, so it is a warrant-strength defect rather than a count-discipline breach. Separately and more concretely, the same sentence appeals to what 'this campaign otherwise treats' - a governance-process appeal that row prose should not carry in any field. REFINED on the unweighed-counter-reading arm: the row DOES weigh the merge - its strongest_rejected_alternative is precisely that reading, and it notes the shared destination itself. What is genuinely missing is the grammatical arm, that the waw on both onsets is a sequencing form which reads at least as readily as one continuing announcement. Correct as written: the quoted run reaches byte tier, and the SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.27.11 and after oshb:Isa.27.12 are correctly typed, correctly keyed to the Hebrew witness, and disclosed single-witness and non-driving.
boundary_proposals.remedy: (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: delete the appeal to campaign practice and to the header class; re-warrant the split from this row's own bytes - the two onsets agree at accent_stripped tier and differ at byte tier, each opens a distinct image, and a single-witness setumah stands between them (tier-3, non-driving) - and add one clause weighing the sequencing reading of the waw rather than leaving it unanswered. (2) boundary_rationale: give the onset formula a tier and a digit with its unit named (the long form at 13 verses book-wide at skeleton tier), and distinguish it from the bare form so the signal key is not carrying two spellings. No boundary change proposed. TESTS: no field appeals to campaign practice, a governing document, or a device class the row is not itself using; every recurrence claim names a tier and carries a digit with its unit; the word 'identical' appears only where a byte-tier collation supports it.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The row closes the book's 27:13|28:1 frame seam without quoting the frame form that makes it a seam, and explains the missing mark there with a generalization the mark inventory contradicts.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Both arms verify exactly. ARM 1: the closing seam is argued from the parent grouping ('the closing verse of its book-level parent grouping, so this row's own close is fixed by that larger seam') and from the row's own onset, never from the following verse's bytes. web:Isa.28.1 appears as a bare reference with no oshb: counterpart anywhere in the row, and the form that makes 28:1 a seam - the verse-initial ה֗וֹי (oshb:Isa.28.1, byte tier), a member of the 20-site verse-initial woe inventory - is never quoted. A frame-based seam claim owes the frame form and its role in the cited verse's own bytes. The asymmetry is visible across the seam pair: the Isa.28.1-Isa.28.13 row on the other side of this very join DOES quote that form byte-true. ARM 2: the row states that no mark follows Isa.27.13 and that this is 'expected since it is the book's own frame-seam verse'. The absence itself is TRUE - the parashah inventory records no petuchah or setumah at MT 27:13 - but the explanation is contradicted by the inventory. Of the eight verses that close a parent grouping in this architecture, FIVE carry a mark - petuchah at MT 12:6, MT 35:10 and MT 39:8; setumah at MT 48:22 and MT 55:13 - and only MT 1:1, MT 27:13 and MT 66:24 do not. Every digit in the challenge checks out. So a tier-3 absence is given explanatory work on a layer where absence is never evidence in either direction, and the generalization it is given is false besides. CLARIFICATION, not a defect: MT 27:13 does carry one paseq seg (single-witness, count-only). That is a different layer with no symmetry obligation, so its non-mention is not a gap - but the row's flat 'no mark in the inventory' wording should not be read as covering it. Correct as written: the row's own onset run and its trumpet run both match oshb:Isa.27.13 at byte tier, and the setumah after MT 27:12 at the front seam is correctly typed and correctly keyed to the Hebrew witness.
boundary_proposals.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: splice ה֗וֹי (oshb:Isa.28.1, byte tier) into the closing-seam sentence, name its role as a verse-initial woe onset opening the next series, and add oshb:Isa.28.1 to boundary_evidence_refs, so the seam is engaged in the bytes on both sides of the join. The parent-grouping close may stay as corroboration but cannot be the only warrant. (2) device_notes: cut the explanatory clause 'which is expected since it is the book's own frame-seam verse'. State the absence flatly as a single-witness, tier-3 observation that is not treated as evidence in either direction, or drop the sentence entirely. No boundary change proposed - the seam is fixed architecture. TESTS: the seam claim carries a pointed splice from oshb:Isa.28.1 that re-collates at byte tier; the reference mirror shows oshb:Isa.28.1 present in boundary_evidence_refs; no field assigns explanatory or structural meaning to the absence of a parashah mark.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The row declines an internal cut at 28:5 without disclosing that the verse opens with the very day-formula treated as a unit onset four times in the immediately preceding chapter and that the mark layer brackets exactly the rejected pair, while the counter-argument that holds it in is made from the English with no quoted form and no tier; the remnant and plene/defective observations are likewise unquoted, and all four mark references are written under a WEB coordinate prefix.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Every arm verifies, and the severity is right. ARM 1, the core: oshb:Isa.28.5 opens בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (byte tier) - the same bare verse-initial formula that this cluster's own preceding rows treat as a unit-opening driver at MT 27:1 and MT 27:2, and in its waw-prefixed long form at MT 27:12 and MT 27:13 - and the parashah inventory records a SAMEKH after MT 28:4 and another after MT 28:6, bracketing PRECISELY the 28:5-28:6 pair the row declines to cut. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative is a single sentence naming the rival and neither of its corroborations, so the strongest reading against the row's own choice is stated at its weakest. Both marks do appear in boundary_evidence_refs, so the disclosure layer is complete; what is missing is the connection between them and the rival they support. ARM 2: the argument that holds the pair inside the span - that the crown motif keeps running - is made from “a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty to the residue of his people” (web:Isa.28.5) with no quoted form and no tier, although the byte evidence is strong and available: לַעֲטֶ֣רֶת צְבִ֔י (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier) is the third of exactly 3 sites of the crown noun in this chapter and 4 book-wide (sweep: 4 verses at skeleton tier - oshb:Isa.28.1, oshb:Isa.28.3, oshb:Isa.28.5, oshb:Isa.62.3). ARM 3: the remnant identification is English-only too - לִשְׁאָ֖ר עַמּֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier) is the plain remnant noun, and the row's own signal key names the remnant family, an object this book splits four ways on one root, so the form owes its bytes. ARM 4: the plene/defective observation in device_notes is byte-true and unquoted - שִׁכֹּרֵ֣י (oshb:Isa.28.1, byte tier) against שִׁכּוֹרֵ֥י (oshb:Isa.28.3, byte tier). A spelling claim is a byte-checkable claim under the same discipline as a digit. ARM 5: all four mark references are written under a WEB coordinate prefix although the parashah layer is read from the Hebrew witness and keyed to its numbering; the arithmetic lands only because this chapter is identity-numbered, and the immediately preceding rows key the same object correctly at MT 26:21, MT 27:1, MT 27:6, MT 27:11 and MT 27:12. This is model territory, not a machine catch - the staged sweeps pass on these rows - which is why it needs recording: the same habit inside either offset zone would be a Tier-0 disclosure failure. Correct as written, and independently confirmed: the crown pair the row does quote is handled right - עֲטֶ֤רֶת גֵּאוּת֙ and עֲטֶ֥רֶת גֵּא֖וּת differ at byte tier and agree once accents are stripped, exactly as the row labels it; the woe onset at the row's own front edge IS quoted byte-true, which is the half of this seam pair that the Isa.27.13 row omits. POLICY NOTE for routing, not a ruling: whether a bare day-formula onset cuts a row INSIDE a hoy-onset complex is not settled by the operative rules - the formula is not a member of the staged tier-1 frame spine, and the woe category carries no internal-cut rule of its own. That reading is boss territory; the work order below is disclosure only.
boundary_proposals.remedy: (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: rebuild the rival at full strength before rejecting it - splice בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier), name the SAMEKH after MT 28:4 and after MT 28:6 as bracketing exactly that pair (tier-3, single-witness, non-driving), and then give the reason the pair stays in. (2) boundary_rationale: replace the English-only crown and remnant arms with splices - לַעֲטֶ֣רֶת צְבִ֔י and לִשְׁאָ֖ר עַמּֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier) - carrying the crown noun's digit and unit (sweep: 4 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, 3 in this chapter) and naming which remnant object of the four is meant. (3) device_notes: quote both spellings in the plene/defective sentence, שִׁכֹּרֵ֣י against שִׁכּוֹרֵ֥י, with the tier named. (4) Re-key all four mark references to the Hebrew witness (oshb:) to match the layer they are read from and the preceding rows' practice. No boundary change proposed here; any actual cut at 28:5-28:6 is a proposal for boss adoption, never author work. TESTS: the rejected alternative names every corroboration the bytes and the inventory supply for the reading it rejects; every device, spelling, and remnant claim carries a pointed splice re-collating at byte tier plus a tier label; every parashah reference in the row is keyed to the Hebrew witness; the crown digit names its unit and its tier.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: LF: the high confidence understates the live rival at the Isa.28.16 koh-amar frame, which the row rejects with only a generic addressee-continuity claim rather than the stronger subordinating evidence available in the bytes. OL: both of the row's edge arguments are made without any Hebrew, the label it puts on its close-seam verse is contradicted by that verse's bytes, and the same object takes two witness keys in one reference list.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT in what they touch - LF the internal rival and the confidence band, OL the two edges and the reference keys - but they share ONE root cause, which neither packet names: this row systematically splices past the causal connector that opens the verse it is quoting. LF UPHELD on substance: oshb:Isa.28.16 opens לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ (byte tier), and the row's splice begins at the messenger formula, dropping the particle. That particle is the stronger warrant the row does not use - it ties the divine reply directly to the covenant-with-death quotation of 28:15 as its answer - while the reason actually given for declining the rival cut is a generic 'same addressee and frame carry through'. REFINED on the second half: the confidence comparison with neighbouring rows is factually accurate (the Isa.28.1-Isa.28.13 row sits at medium, the Isa.27.6-Isa.27.11 row at medium_low) but band-consistency with neighbours is not itself a rule; the curable defect is the omitted particle and the generic rival wording, and the confidence band follows from repairing those. OL UPHELD, with one tier sharpened. Front seam: it is the row's strongest signal and carries no byte arm at all - the bytes give שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָצ֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.28.14, byte tier), the addressee standing in the last two of those tokens, and that full summons formula stands at 3 verses book-wide at SKELETON tier (sweep: 3 verses - MT 1:10, MT 28:14, MT 66:5) and at 2 verses at byte tier (MT 1:10, MT 28:14); the challenge's digit is right for the skeleton object and the tier belongs with it. Close seam: the row describes 28:23 as 'a fresh vocative onset', but oshb:Isa.28.23 reads הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אִמְרָתִֽי (byte tier) - six tokens, four imperative forms and two objects, no addressee noun and no vocative particle - so the label sits on a verse whose bytes do not carry it. Unclaimed bracket: the scoffer root does frame the span end to end, לָצ֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.28.14) against אַל תִּתְלוֹצָ֔צוּ (oshb:Isa.28.22), each byte tier and each standing at exactly 1 verse book-wide - a root-level link across two attested spellings, correctly cited per spelling by the challenge and not a byte-true recurrence. Keys: web:Isa.28.13 and web:Isa.28.15 carry the parashah citations while oshb:Isa.28.15 carries the ketiv/qere citation in the same list - the SAME verse under two witness keys for two objects both read from the Hebrew witness. NEW FINDING neither packet reached: the connector-eliding habit also operates at the row's OWN front edge, where it matters most. oshb:Isa.28.14 opens לָכֵ֛ן (byte tier) and the English reads “Therefore hear Yahweh’s word, you scoffers, that rule this people in Jerusalem:” (web:Isa.28.14) - the row's quotation starts after 'Therefore'. A backward-pointing causal connector at the opening verse argues continuity with the material closing at 28:13, and the row's 'a fresh addressee opens this row' claim never engages it. The petuchah after MT 28:13 corroborates a break on tier-3 weak grounds but cannot carry that argument by itself. Correct as written: the one Hebrew run the row does quote is byte-true and its speaker class is named as divine, which is the right discipline on a formula this book uses on both a divine and a royal-messenger side; the doubled ketiv/qere at MT 28:15 is disclosed and kept out of quotation.
boundary_proposals.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale, front seam: splice לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָצ֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.28.14, byte tier) INCLUDING the causal connector, add oshb:Isa.28.14 to boundary_evidence_refs, carry the summons-formula digit with its unit and tier (sweep: 3 verses book-wide at skeleton tier), and state why the backward-pointing connector does not bind this verse to the unit closing at 28:13. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut the internal rival so it engages לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ (oshb:Isa.28.16, byte tier) with the particle included, and re-check the confidence band once the rival is stated at full strength. (3) boundary_rationale, close: drop the 'vocative' label - the bytes at oshb:Isa.28.23 give an imperative-summons onset; re-key the signal accordingly, and note the scoffer-root bracket per attested spelling, explicitly NOT as a byte-true recurrence. (4) Re-key the two parashah references to the Hebrew witness so the whole list reads on one witness. No boundary change proposed. TESTS: every Hebrew splice in the row begins at the head of the clause it is quoting, connector included, and re-collates at byte tier; no form-class or speech-class label is applied to a verse whose bytes do not carry the form; every parashah and ketiv/qere reference in the row is keyed to the Hebrew witness; the confidence band is re-derived after the rival is restated.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The summons the row builds its onset and its type on is quoted only in half, the vocative label it records is not present in that verse's bytes, and the disputation evidence actually inside the span goes uncited.
boundary_proposals.grounds: All four arms verify. ARM 1: the row states that 'the Hebrew doubles the summons verb pair' and then splices only הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י (oshb:Isa.28.23, byte tier). The doubling lives in the unquoted second colon, הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אִמְרָתִֽי (oshb:Isa.28.23, byte tier); the full verse is הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אִמְרָתִֽי. The run actually cited displays one pair, not the doubling claimed for it - a quote that does not carry the feature it is offered as evidence for. ARM 2: the recorded signal and the rationale both call the onset a vocative, but oshb:Isa.28.23's six tokens are four imperative forms and two objects, with no addressee noun and no vocative particle; the row's own English, “Give ear, and hear my voice! Listen, and hear my speech!” (web:Isa.28.23), carries none either. An imperative-summons onset is what the bytes give, and a form-class label is a byte-checkable claim. ARM 3: the type rests on that summons form alone, and the form is not distinctive - it stands at 5 verses book-wide at skeleton tier (sweep: 5 verses - MT 1:10, MT 8:9, MT 28:23, MT 51:4, and MT 64:3 = web:Isa.64.4, the dual correctly carried by the challenge in the offset zone) - spread across openings of very different speech classes, so it under-determines the applied category on its own. ARM 4: the evidence that would carry the typing sits inside the row's own span and is uncited - the verse-initial interrogatives הֲכֹ֣ל (oshb:Isa.28.24, byte tier) and הֲלוֹא֙ (oshb:Isa.28.25, byte tier) open the case the row says the unit is making. MITIGATING, and worth recording against the severity: this row DOES carry the operative-category deviation disclosure its label requires, argued on formal rather than subject-matter ground, and it holds itself at reduced confidence with its frontier flag set - the honest posture. The defect is that the formal ground it names is quoted in half and the in-span evidence that would settle it is left out, not that the label was taken carelessly. Correct as written: the close against the following woe onset is byte-defensible, and the SAMEKH after MT 28:29 is correctly typed as single-witness - though it too is keyed to the WEB witness rather than to the Hebrew one the layer is read from, the same keying defect this writer part carries across its rows.
boundary_proposals.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: extend the splice to the whole verse, הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אִמְרָתִֽי (oshb:Isa.28.23, byte tier), so the run displays the doubling the row claims for it. (2) Replace the vocative label with an imperative-summons onset in the prose AND in the recorded signal key, since no addressee noun or vocative particle stands in the verse. (3) Add the in-span typing evidence: splice הֲכֹ֣ל (oshb:Isa.28.24) and הֲלוֹא֙ (oshb:Isa.28.25), both byte tier, as the verse-initial interrogatives that carry the disputation reading, and add both refs; carry the summons form's digit with its unit and tier (sweep: 5 verses book-wide at skeleton tier), disclosing that the form alone does not fix the category. Keep the existing deviation disclosure. (4) Re-key the parashah reference to the Hebrew witness. No boundary change and no unit_type change proposed. TESTS: every quoted run displays the feature it is cited for; no form-class or speech-class label survives that the cited verse's bytes do not carry; the typing sentence cites at least one in-span form with a tier; the parashah reference is keyed to the Hebrew witness.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: A clause repeated at consonantal-skeleton tier across the row's own rear seam is left undisclosed while the row records high confidence, and the rival reading is stated without its byte grounds.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Verified from bytes, and the challenge's tier discrimination is exactly right -- the sharpest item in the cluster. The run עַל עַ֖ם לֹא יוֹעִ֣ילוּ stands at oshb:Isa.30.5 (byte tier) followed by לָ֑מוֹ, and oshb:Isa.30.6 ends on עַל עַ֖ם לֹ֥א יוֹעִֽילוּ (byte tier). Re-swept independently at all three tiers, the two meet at consonantal-skeleton tier and at NO higher tier, and at that tier the clause is attested in exactly 2 verses book-wide, oshb:Isa.30.5 and oshb:Isa.30.6. The accent-stripped tier separates them (1 verse) because the second site retains meteg where the first carries cantillation -- the challenge's tier call survives the check. Its count-object is the shared run, not the longer oshb:Isa.30.5 clause it also quotes; the quoted clause and the swept string differ, which is a presentation looseness in the challenge and not a count-object error. The Egypt naming crosses the same seam and verifies: מִצְרַ֖יִם and its attested byform spellings stand at oshb:Isa.30.2 and oshb:Isa.30.3 inside the span and at oshb:Isa.30.7 beyond it -- 40 verses book-wide at consonantal-skeleton tier, in chapters 28-31 at Isa.30.2, Isa.30.3, Isa.30.7, Isa.31.1, Isa.31.3. It is the weaker of the two because it skips the header verse itself. The row records HIGH confidence and its strongest_rejected_alternative names the extend-through-Isa.30.7 rival in a bare sentence with no byte ground at all, so the strongest counter-evidence to its own cut appears nowhere in the row. Under the cross-seam rule an undisclosed device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against it, and here that lands on the top confidence band. Credited and verified: ה֣וֹי בָּנִ֤ים סֽוֹרְרִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.30.1 (byte tier), a woe onset with the postpositive signature attached; the tier-3 setumah at Isa.30.5 matches the single-witness inventory under the correct type; and the row's variant-note slicing statement is accurate.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author wave. (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut so the rival carries its actual textual ground -- the clause repeated across Isa.30.5|Isa.30.6, named at consonantal-skeleton tier with its 2-verse book-wide digit -- instead of a bare assertion, using the sanctioned optional second sentence for the rival disclosure. (2) Add the cross-seam disclosure to boundary_rationale or device_notes with the tier named, and add oshb:Isa.30.5 and oshb:Isa.30.6 to boundary_evidence_refs. (3) confidence: re-decide after the disclosure lands. High is not defensible while the strongest counter-evidence to the cut is absent from the row; the cut itself stands on the verse-initial header at oshb:Isa.30.6, so it is the band that moves, not the span -- this remedy proposes no boundary change. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: one half of a SEAM PAIR with P08-009 at the same Isa.30.5|Isa.30.6 edge -- ONE edit, matching wording and matching tier label on both rows. Cure test -- the test that killed the original: a book-wide sweep of the shared run at all three tiers must appear in the row with the skeleton tier named and the 2-verse digit stated, and no sentence may describe the rival as merely thematic.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The row cuts correctly on a verse-initial burden header but describes the rival as thematic when the bytes repeat a clause across that seam, understating the counter-weight on a low-band hold.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The defect is real and byte-confirmed, but the severity is one band too high for this row. Verified: the same skeleton-tier repetition adjudicated on P08-008 crosses this row's FRONT seam -- עַל עַ֖ם לֹא יוֹעִ֣ילוּ at oshb:Isa.30.5 against עַל עַ֖ם לֹ֥א יוֹעִֽילוּ closing oshb:Isa.30.6 (both byte tier as spliced), meeting only at consonantal-skeleton tier, exactly 2 verses book-wide. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative rests the rival on shared Egypt-reliance subject-matter and the absence of an addressee shift; the bytes give lexical repetition, a materially higher grade of counter-evidence than theme. The challenge's finding is correct. Also verified, all credited to the row: מַשָּׂ֖א בַּהֲמ֣וֹת נֶ֑גֶב is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.30.6 (byte tier) and is the construct-header form, correctly kept apart from the burden common noun וְכֹ֖בֶד at oshb:Isa.30.27. The skeleton is attested at 15 verses book-wide of which exactly 10 are verse-initial headers, so the row's 10-header digit and the challenge's role-split both check out against a contiguous-substring sweep that would otherwise blend the three roles. The rear-seam opener עַתָּ֗ה בּ֣וֹא at oshb:Isa.30.8 is unique in the book (1 verse at consonantal-skeleton tier), and the tier-3 setumah at Isa.30.5 matches the single-witness inventory. SEVERITY REFINED medium to low, on the row's own exposure. Unlike its seam partner this row does NOT record high confidence: it is held at medium_low, it names the header-inside-woe-zone tension in device_notes rather than suppressing it, and it discloses the continuity rival in substance. What is wrong is the GRADE assigned to that rival, not its absence. A disclosure that exists but understates its evidentiary tier on an already-hedged low-band row is a prose-completeness defect, not a position-endangering one -- and the asymmetry with P08-008, where the identical device is absent entirely at the top band, is the calibration this pair needs.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author wave, and this is the SAME EDIT as the P08-008 remedy, not a second one -- seam-pair law. In strongest_rejected_alternative, replace the thematic ground with the textual one: the closing clause of the header verse repeats the clause the preceding verse turns on, at consonantal-skeleton tier, attested in exactly 2 verses book-wide. Keep the formal-header ground for the cut, which is untouched; no boundary change is proposed. Add oshb:Isa.30.5 to boundary_evidence_refs. Cure test: the rival sentence must name a tier and carry a digit, and the same tier label and digit must appear on both rows of the pair.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: OL: the messenger-frame and divine-title signals are asserted from the English rendering, without a pointed form, a tier or a named frame owner -- at the one site in the span where the frame is owned by a non-adjacent title. LF: the row folds the koh-amar citations into the unit's texture without stating which speech-frame class they carry, leaving the frame identification implicit in the adjacent title.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The SAME defect from both lenses -- the frame class is never named -- with OL strictly the broader statement of it. Adjudicated as one, at OL's severity, which subsumes LF's. Verified from bytes: the two frames are לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל at oshb:Isa.30.12 and כִּ֣י כֹֽה אָמַר֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל at oshb:Isa.30.15 (byte tier), both divine. The row quotes neither in Hebrew: its boundary_evidence_refs carry oshb:Isa.30.8 alone, every other cited site being a web: ref, so two declared substrate signals -- the messenger-formula key and the divine-title key -- rest on English quotations with no pointed form and no tier. OL's sharpest point verifies, and is why this outranks LF's low band: at oshb:Isa.30.12 the frame's owner IS the title, with no adjacent divine name in the clause -- precisely the configuration this book's messenger-formula census is role-split to catch, since an unnamed owner there cannot be checked at all, whereas at oshb:Isa.30.15 the divine name stands inside the frame itself. LF's inference that the adjacent title marks the class is right in result but is exactly the implicit reasoning the naming rule exists to forbid. The title digit verifies: the three in-span sites are אֶת קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל at oshb:Isa.30.11 and the title standing inside each of the two frames (byte tier) -- correct against the 25-verse book-wide inventory, whose chapters-28-31 members are Isa.29.19, Isa.30.11, Isa.30.12, Isa.30.15, Isa.31.1. OL's third observation verifies and is correctly kept below severity: בּ֣וֹא כָתְבָ֥הּ at oshb:Isa.30.8 (byte tier) is second-person masculine SINGULAR against the plural marking around it, so the singular-versus-plural contrast the row's onset rests on is byte-supported, but the verse names no addressee, so the row's assignment of the commission to the prophet is an inference the cited verse does not carry. Credited: the opener עַתָּ֗ה בּ֣וֹא is unique in the book (1 verse at consonantal-skeleton tier), and both in-span marked divisions are disclosed under the correct, unconflated types -- a setumah at Isa.30.11 and a petuchah at Isa.30.14 -- matching the single-witness inventory.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author wave, one pass. (1) boundary_rationale: splice both frames pointed from source with their oshb: refs and name the tier, and state the frame class explicitly as divine for each -- at oshb:Isa.30.12 naming the title AS the frame owner, since no adjacent divine name stands there. (2) Splice the title at oshb:Isa.30.11 pointed with its tier rather than quoting three English renderings; or demote the title to device_notes as texture and drop its substrate-signal key, which then re-opens unit_type and confidence as dependent fields. (3) Add oshb:Isa.30.11, oshb:Isa.30.12 and oshb:Isa.30.15 to boundary_evidence_refs. (4) Soften the prophet-referent assertion at oshb:Isa.30.8 to what the verse carries -- a second-person singular commission against the surrounding plural, referent not named in the verse. No boundary change is proposed. Cure test -- the test that killed the original: every declared substrate signal in the row must be traceable to a pointed splice with a named tier and an oshb: ref, and no messenger-formula citation may stand without naming whose frame it is.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The row's opener is a consequence connector rather than a temporal turn, and the speaking voice changes at the front seam instead of continuing -- so both stated grounds fail even though the boundary itself is sound; and the in-span paseq at Isa.30.25 is omitted while the row engages the marked-division layer.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Both stated grounds are byte-false and the disclosure gap is real; the challenge's conclusion -- the boundary is better supported than the row argues -- also verifies. Ground one: oshb:Isa.30.18 opens וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽחֲנַנְכֶ֔ם (byte tier) and carries the same particle a second time later in the verse, with no temporal element anywhere in it. Re-swept independently and word-bound to guard against substring bleed, the bare particle stands at exactly 25 verses book-wide at consonantal-skeleton tier -- 23 bare plus 2 with the conjunction, the contiguous-substring and word-bound digits agreeing -- and within chapters 29-30 at Isa.29.14, Isa.29.22, Isa.30.7, Isa.30.12, Isa.30.13 and Isa.30.18, the same form לָכֵ֗ן that opens the indictment frame at oshb:Isa.30.12. It is this book's consequence connector; the row's temporal-turn label is byte-false. Ground two: the verses the row turns from are divine speech under the frame at oshb:Isa.30.15 addressing second-person plural -- גְּבֽוּרַתְכֶ֑ם and אֲבִיתֶֽם at oshb:Isa.30.15, תָּנֻ֑סוּ and נוֹתַרְתֶּ֗ם at oshb:Isa.30.17 (byte tier) -- while oshb:Isa.30.18 names the deity in the third person. The speaking voice does change at the front seam, so the same-voice ground fails. REFINEMENT the challenge does not supply and the cure needs: the ADDRESSEE does continue across that seam, oshb:Isa.30.18's second-person plural object suffixes answering the second-person plural of oshb:Isa.30.15 and oshb:Isa.30.17 (byte tier). The continuity the row was reaching for exists; it was attached to the wrong grammatical category. That converts the finding from a wholesale loss of ground into a correctable restatement, and it is what the replacement warrant should rest on. Disclosure gap verified: a paseq seg stands at Isa.30.25, inside the span, and is the only paseq in chapters 29-30 (the next is Isa.31.4). The row engages the marked-division layer at Isa.30.18 and Isa.30.26 -- both setumah, both matching the single-witness inventory under the correct type -- and omits it. The machine arms do not catch this, which is why it needs the model pass; the neighbouring rows in this corpus do disclose their in-span paseq as presence-only, so the row is asymmetric with its own corpus.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author wave. (1) boundary_rationale: replace the fresh-temporal-turn label with the consequence-connector reading, naming the particle's tier and its digit, and noting it is the same connector that opens the indictment frame earlier in the chapter. (2) Replace the same-speaking-voice ground with the byte-true one: the speaker turns from divine first-person speech to third-person report while the second-person plural ADDRESSEE continues unbroken across the seam -- that is the continuity the unit actually has. (3) Add the in-span paseq disclosure as presence only, single-witness, with no position claim. (4) Add oshb:Isa.30.15, oshb:Isa.30.17 and the paseq site to boundary_evidence_refs. (5) observed_substrate_signals: the reversal-onset key is a driver label the corrected reading changes; re-check it, and with it unit_type, confidence and strongest_rejected_alternative. No boundary change is proposed -- the challenge and this ruling both find the cut better supported than the row argues. Cure test -- the test that killed the original: the row must contain no temporal claim about oshb:Isa.30.18 and no same-speaker claim across Isa.30.17|Isa.30.18; a person-form scan must place the speaker change at that seam and the addressee continuity across it; and a span-relevant disclosure sweep of the row must return every marked division AND the paseq site with nothing left over.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The row's apparatus work inside its own span is asymmetric -- it engages one of the two variant-note verses it covers, attributes the segment marks to the wrong witness, and leaves a two-site catchword hooking across its rear edge undisclosed.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Two of the three limbs verify; the middle limb is REFUTED on the bytes and on the campaign's own ref contract, and with it removed the severity does not hold. UPHELD, limb 1: the variant-note inventory places notes at exactly two verses inside this span, oshb:Isa.30.32 and oshb:Isa.30.33. The row engages only the second, and engages it actively -- it makes a positional slicing claim there, which verifies: the doubled pair גַּם הוא הִ֛יא stands early in oshb:Isa.30.33, well ahead of the verse-final clause the row quotes. The first note, staged the same way as נִלְחַם בה בָּֽם at oshb:Isa.30.32 with its unpointed member at skeleton grade, is nowhere disclosed. A span that actively works one variant note owes the others it covers; the asymmetry is real. REFUTED, limb 2: the row's mark citations read web:Isa.30.26 with setumah and single-witness, and web:Isa.30.33 with setumah and single-witness. Both are the sanctioned form, not a witness misattribution. The campaign's ref-validation contract crosswalk-maps web: refs to MT keys BEFORE the mark-inventory lookup and requires only that the claimed TYPE match the bytes and that single-witness disclosure be present in the field. Both are satisfied: the inventory carries SAMEKH at Isa.30.26 and SAMEKH at Isa.30.33, correctly typed and never conflated with the petuchah class; chapter 30 is identity numbering so no dual is owed; and the consolidated ref arm and mark-symmetry arm over this corpus both return clean with zero problems. The alleged seam-pair disagreement is a bare PREFIX difference between two sanctioned spellings of the same claim, and the mixed convention runs through the whole draft corpus and through both primaries' own packets, so it cannot be charged as a per-row defect here. Witness identity is disclosed by the single-witness tag, which is present; the prefix marks the coordinate space, not the scribal witness. UPHELD, limb 3: the cross-seam hook verifies exactly -- הֶעְמִ֣יק at oshb:Isa.30.33 and הֶעְמִ֥יקוּ at oshb:Isa.31.6 share an unpointed letter string attested at exactly 2 verses book-wide, the word-bound re-check returning the same 2, both flanking this rear edge. Undisclosed, and the challenge correctly declines to make it overturn the cut. Credited and verified: the onset splice הִנֵּ֤ה שֵׁם יְהוָה֙ בָּ֣א matches oshb:Isa.30.27 byte for byte, and the challenge's unforced credit is sound -- מִמֶּרְחָ֔ק at oshb:Isa.30.27 is answered by בֹּעֲרָ֖ה inside the very clause quoted at oshb:Isa.30.33, a root-level inclusio across two distinct attested spellings running the span's own length, which the row does not use. SEVERITY REFINED medium to low. With the witness charge struck, what remains is two disclosure debts. Neither touches the boundary, neither trips a validator arm, the row's own positional variant-note claim is byte-true, and the challenge itself concedes the bounds are better supported than the row argues. Low is the honest band.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author wave, limbs 1 and 3 only -- do NOT act on the witness-prefix charge, which is refuted; changing the prefixes would be churn against a sanctioned form. (1) device_notes: disclose the second in-span variant note at oshb:Isa.30.32 alongside the one already named, presence only, single-witness, no reading adjudicated. (2) Add the rear-edge catchword disclosure naming the two flanking sites, the unpointed-string tier and the 2-verse book-wide digit, retaining the row's existing statement that the woe onset and the marked division at that edge carry the cut. (3) Optional strengthening of boundary_rationale with the span-length root-level inclusio, spliced pointed from both verses with the root-level relation named across the two attested spellings -- a free warrant the row is leaving on the table. Add oshb:Isa.30.32, oshb:Isa.30.33 and oshb:Isa.31.6 to boundary_evidence_refs. No boundary change is proposed. Cure test: a variant-note sweep scoped to the row's own span must return both covered verses disclosed with nothing left over -- the symmetry test the original failed -- and any recurrence claim across the rear edge must name its tier and its digit.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: This row's span is the whole of chapter 31 (all nine verses), and its medium confidence sits one band above the ceiling the campaign holds for any whole-chapter span.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Verified independently from both witnesses' keyed verse maps: chapter 31 carries exactly 9 verses in WEB and exactly 9 in MT, and the row's span runs Isa.31.1-Isa.31.9 -- the complete chapter, with no offset in play (chapter 31 is identity numbering). The row records medium. The campaign caps whole-chapter spans at medium_low, so this is a one-band overshoot, and this row is a named member of the cross-batch whole-chapter class. The challenge is correctly scoped to calibration alone, and that scoping verifies: the seam warrant is genuinely sound and I could not dislodge it. ה֣וֹי is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.31.1 (byte tier) and is the fifth of exactly 6 verse-initial woe onsets across chapters 28-33; the divine frame כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר יְהוָ֣ה at oshb:Isa.31.4 (byte tier) names the deity as speaker inside its own clause, so it is a divine frame and not one of this book's four royal-messenger uses of the formula; the postpositive שָׂרָ֑יו נְאֻם at oshb:Isa.31.9 (byte tier) is mid-verse and correctly characterised as a signature rather than an onset. Apparatus disclosure verifies as complete for the span -- the marks at oshb:Isa.31.3 and oshb:Isa.31.9, the front-seam mark at oshb:Isa.30.33, all SAMEKH and all correctly typed and unconflated against the single-witness inventory, the paseq at oshb:Isa.31.4 tallied as presence and not placement, and no variant note falls anywhere in chapter 31. So the defect is the band and only the band. Medium severity is right: one band, on a row whose evidence is otherwise the strongest in this cluster.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author wave. (1) confidence: medium to medium_low. This is NOT a one-character edit -- dropping into the low band triggers the campaign's low-band machinery, so the same pass must add the medium_low mirroring across all three sidecars with full schemas (why_low_confidence, concern_type, possible_downstream_risk, suggested_reviewer, proposed_atlas_action, promotion authorities, review states) and a frontier-queue row for this chunk. Write the why_low_confidence text bespoke to the whole-chapter extent, not boilerplate. (2) Bundle into the same pass the two sub-threshold disclosure debts the other lens raised without charging them, since they touch the same fields: splice the imperative address at oshb:Isa.31.6 pointed, שׁ֗וּבוּ לַאֲשֶׁ֛ר הֶעְמִ֥יקוּ סָרָ֖ה בְּנֵ֥י (byte tier), rather than naming it from the English; and disclose the front-seam hook where הֶעְמִ֣יק at oshb:Isa.30.33 and הֶעְמִ֥יקוּ at oshb:Isa.31.6 share an unpointed letter string attested at exactly 2 verses book-wide, with the tier and digit named. Add oshb:Isa.31.6 to boundary_evidence_refs. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: that hook is a SEAM PAIR at the Isa.30.33|Isa.31.1 edge -- it is the same crossing I upheld from the other side on P08-012 in the preceding attempt. ONE edit across the two rows, matching tier label and matching digit; do not let the two halves be cured separately with divergent wording. No boundary change is proposed on either row. Cure test: a whole-chapter check over the row's span must find the confidence at or below medium_low, and every low-band sidecar and frontier-queue obligation satisfied for this chunk -- the band edit alone does not pass.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The onset rests entirely on the English rendering of a particle the row never quotes, the same verse-initial particle is treated as non-structural elsewhere in this same stretch, and the variant note inside the span is undisclosed.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The core finding is right and is upheld; two of the three limbs need their framing corrected, and the severity is confirmed rather than moved. UPHELD, and this is the real defect: the row carries no pointed Hebrew anywhere. Its only oshb: refs are the two mark citations, so nothing in it is spliced. What its front seam actually rests on is a topic description read off the English, the preceding unit's closing signature named but never spliced, and tier-3 marks on both sides -- and it records HIGH confidence on that. Under the evidence policy a boundary grounded only on a marker is defective, and tier-3 parashah is never a driver; so the front seam has no tier-1 signal argued in the bytes at all. That is an engagement-class breach carrying a top-band row. FRAMING CORRECTED, limb 1: the challenge says the onset rests on the English rendering of a particle. It does not -- the row never invokes a particle in any form; the presentative is the challenge's own supply of the Hebrew the row should have engaged. That is a legitimate move, but stated as written it credits the row with a driver it does not claim. The particle is genuinely there: oshb:Isa.32.1 opens הֵ֥ן (byte tier), verse-initial at exactly 18 verses book-wide (re-swept independently), so the cure is cheap and the boundary will very likely survive it. FRAMING CORRECTED, limb 2: the cross-site inconsistency verifies exactly -- the only two verse-initial sites of that particle across chapters 28-35 are oshb:Isa.32.1 and הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם at oshb:Isa.33.7 -- but it is not a defect PRESENT in this row, because this row does not use the particle. boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The front edge is contested by the bytes on three independent counts: the clause chain runs across it, the register change cited to justify it is not located there, and the alternative it rejects is the one the lexical evidence supports.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Every count verifies from bytes, every digit and every count-object survives an independent re-derivation, and the row carries no pointed Hebrew at all. This is the strongest challenge in either of my clusters. Count 1 verifies: oshb:Isa.32.16 opens וְשָׁכַ֥ן (byte tier), a waw-plus-perfect continuing ר֖וּחַ מִמָּר֑וֹם וְהָיָ֤ה at oshb:Isa.32.15 inside the same subordinate clause opened by עַד יֵ֨עָרֶ֥ה; nothing verse-initial marks a fresh start. The English adverb at that verse renders the waw form and not an adverb in the text -- re-swept independently, the Hebrew adverb אָ֥ז (oshb:Isa.35.5, byte tier) stands verse-initial at exactly 6 verses book-wide and oshb:Isa.32.16 is not among them. Count 2 verifies exactly, and it is the decisive one because the row's ONLY stated boundary ground is this register change. The last second-person address forms in the stretch are חִרְדוּ֙ שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת and the imperatives following them at oshb:Isa.32.11 (byte tier). A form scan of oshb:Isa.32.12 through oshb:Isa.32.15 returns no second-person form: סֹֽפְדִ֑ים at oshb:Isa.32.12 is a masculine plural participle rendered as an imperative by the English witness alone, oshb:Isa.32.13 carries a first-person singular suffix and a third-person feminine verb, oshb:Isa.32.14 carries none, and oshb:Isa.32.15 carries the first-person plural עָלֵ֛ינוּ. So the address the row says governs through Isa.32.15 in fact stops at Isa.32.11 -- four verses ahead of the cut it is used to justify. The row's sole ground is byte-false in its location. Count 3 verifies: שַׁאֲנַנּֽוֹת at oshb:Isa.32.18 rejoins the token opening oshb:Isa.32.9 and oshb:Isa.32.11 at consonantal-skeleton tier, exactly 3 verses book-wide and byte-identical between the first two; and מִבְטַחִ֔ים at oshb:Isa.32.18 -- attested at exactly 1 verse book-wide, so a genuinely unique form -- answers בֹּֽטח֔וֹת at oshb:Isa.32.9 on the same root, that spelling standing at exactly 3 verses book-wide at consonantal-skeleton tier. The challenge names this a root-level observation across two distinct attested spellings rather than a token match, which is the honest description and exactly the tier discipline the campaign requires. The lexical evidence therefore runs toward the grouping the row rejected. Also verified: the closing formula אַשְׁרֵיכֶ֕ם at oshb:Isa.32.20 is byte-true and unquoted, and the challenge's point about the tier-3 mark at that verse holds -- it corroborates a break there equally well under either grouping, so it cannot arbitrate between them, which is precisely why tier-3 is never a driver. HIGH severity is correct and I decline to move it. The row records medium confidence, argues no Hebrew, rests its entire boundary case on one register claim that the bytes locate four verses away, and the independent lexical evidence positively supports the rival it dismisses. That last element is what separates this from the merely-under-argued rows in this cluster: the evidence does not just fail to support the cut, it points the other way.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author wave, grounds only -- and read the scope limit first. (1) boundary_rationale: strike the claim that the second-person plural address drops after Isa.32.15. A form scan places the last second-person forms at oshb:Isa.32.11, so the sentence is byte-false as written and cannot be repaired by rewording; it must be replaced. If a register ground is still wanted, it must be located where the bytes put it and must then explain why the cut falls where it does and not there. (2) Strike or requalify the temporal reading of the row's opening verse: splice וְשָׁכַ֥ן pointed with its tier, name it as a waw-plus-perfect continuation, and state that the English adverb there renders that form rather than the Hebrew adverb, whose 6 verse-initial sites do not include this verse. (3) strongest_rejected_alternative: the rival is currently dismissed on the ground that is byte-false. Re-cut it to engage the actual counter-evidence -- the clause chain across the edge and the two-site root answer into oshb:Isa.32.18 with its 3-verse and 1-verse digits and its tiers named. (4) Splice the closing formula at oshb:Isa.32.20 pointed with its tier. Add oshb:Isa.32.11, oshb:Isa.32.15, oshb:Isa.32.16, oshb:Isa.32.18 and oshb:Isa.32.20 to boundary_evidence_refs. (5) observed_substrate_signals: the topic-onset key is falsified as stated and the blessing-formula key is unevidenced in Hebrew; both re-open, and with them unit_type and confidence. SCOPE LIMIT, binding: this ruling raises a live question whether Isa.32.16 should open a row at all, given that the clause chain and the lexical answer both run across that edge and that the rejected 32:9-32:20 grouping is what the evidence supports. That is a RESPAN and therefore a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption. It is recorded here as a proposal and is NOT author work; an author must refuse any embedded boundary change and cure the grounds only. The seam is shared with P09-003, so if the boss adopts a respan it lands on both rows as one decision. Cure test -- the test that killed the original: a person-form scan across Isa.32.9-Isa.32.20 must agree with every person claim the row makes, and no boundary ground may be asserted at a verse the scan does not support.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: LF: this row's span is the whole of chapter 34 (all seventeen verses) and its high confidence sits two bands above the whole-chapter ceiling. OL: the row's own onset class recurs verse-initially inside the span at an undisclosed site, no Hebrew is quoted anywhere, and the whole-chapter extent is carried at the top confidence band.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Both are upheld. The two lenses CONVERGE on one defect -- the whole-chapter extent at the top band -- and the other lens adds two distinct findings on top of it. Convergent limb, verified independently from both witnesses' verse maps: chapter 34 carries exactly 17 verses in WEB and exactly 17 in MT, and the span runs Isa.34.1-Isa.34.17, the complete chapter under identity numbering. The row records high against a medium_low ceiling -- a TWO-band overshoot, and this row is a named member of the cross-batch whole-chapter class. Distinct limb A, verified: the row carries no pointed Hebrew anywhere. Its only oshb: ref is a single mark citation; the onset, the addressee shift and the register change at the close are all argued from English renderings. The onset is in fact byte-true -- oshb:Isa.34.1 opens קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ (byte tier), verse-initial imperatives with their vocatives, that imperative standing verse-initial at exactly 3 verses book-wide on an independent re-sweep -- which makes the omission gratuitous rather than difficult. Distinct limb B, verified: the row's negative is written to exclude comparable onsets through the whole chapter, and oshb:Isa.34.16 opens דִּרְשׁ֨וּ מֵֽעַל סֵ֤פֶר יְהוָה֙ וּֽקְרָ֔אוּ (byte tier), a verse-initial imperative pair, that imperative standing verse-initial at exactly 2 verses book-wide with its only other site elsewhere in the book. The other lens is scrupulous here and I confirm the concession: that site carries no vocative, so it is formally weaker than the row's own onset and does not force a cut -- but it is the same imperative-onset class the row uses for itself, and a negative written to exclude that class owes it a disclosure. Credited and verified: apparatus disclosure is complete and correctly typed -- the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.34.17 is the only mark in chapter 34, no paseq and no variant note falls anywhere in the chapter, and the front seam at Isa.33.24 carries no mark, so nothing further is owed. The other lens also makes a fair point that the row's own rejected alternative, weighing a narrowing turn inside the span, is itself evidence that a real internal question was live -- which tells against the top band independently of the cap. HIGH severity. A two-band cap overshoot is on its own the more serious of the two whole-chapter violations I have seen at one band, and the undisclosed interior onset is exactly the exposure the cap exists to price.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author wave, one pass, no boundary change proposed by either lens. (1) confidence: high to medium_low, a two-band drop. As with the other members of this class the band edit alone does not discharge it -- the same pass must add the low-band mirroring across all three sidecars with full schemas and a frontier-queue row for this chunk, with bespoke why_low_confidence text keyed to the whole-chapter extent and to the interior onset below. (2) Splice the onset pointed at oshb:Isa.34.1 with its tier named and its verse-initial digit, so the row's driver rests on the forms rather than on the rendering; add oshb:Isa.34.1 to boundary_evidence_refs. (3) Rewrite the negative so it names the interior imperative onset at oshb:Isa.34.16 rather than excluding it by silence, spliced pointed with its tier and its 2-verse book-wide digit, and states why the row holds across it -- the absence of a vocative there against the vocative-bearing onset at Isa.34.1. Add oshb:Isa.34.16 to boundary_evidence_refs. Cure test -- the test that killed the original: a verse-initial imperative-onset sweep across the row's own span must return oshb:Isa.34.16, and the row must name and address every site it returns; and a whole-chapter check must find the confidence at or below medium_low with the low-band sidecar and frontier-queue obligations satisfied.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: LF: this row's span is the whole of chapter 35 (all ten verses) at high confidence, two bands above the whole-chapter ceiling, and its own closing quotation of Isa.35.10 inserts a stray quotation mark not present in the source. OL: the rejected alternative turns on one English adverb doing two different jobs with no counterpart in the Hebrew, and a second imperative onset inside the span goes unnamed.
boundary_proposals.grounds: Both are upheld. The lenses CONVERGE on the whole-chapter band and each adds a distinct finding the other misses. Convergent limb, verified from both witnesses' verse maps: chapter 35 carries exactly 10 verses in WEB and exactly 10 in MT, and the span runs Isa.35.1-Isa.35.10, the complete chapter under identity numbering, recorded at high against a medium_low ceiling -- a TWO-band overshoot, this row being a named member of the cross-batch whole-chapter class. Distinct limb A, character-level byte-check performed and CONFIRMED. The source verse at web:Isa.35.10 ends on a period followed by exactly one character, U+201D, the curly right double quotation mark closing a speech opened by the U+201C at web:Isa.35.4 and left open across the intervening verses; the source verse contains no U+0022 anywhere. The row's own quotation of that same clause ends on a period, then U+0022, then U+201D -- one straight double-quote character inserted that is absent from the source, and it is the only U+0022 in the row's entire prose. The breach lands on the row's own boundary-closing citation, which is the citation doing the most work in the field. The other lens is right that it does not disturb the seam determination, and right that the close is independently carried. Distinct limb B, verified exactly on an independent re-sweep. The row declines a cut on the ground that the adverb there merely resumes as an earlier one did at Isa.32.16. In the Hebrew these are not the same object: אָ֥ז stands verse-initial at oshb:Isa.35.5 and אָ֣ז again at oshb:Isa.35.6 -- TWO adjacent sites, not the single site the row treats -- and that adverb is verse-initial at exactly 6 verses book-wide, oshb:Isa.32.16 being none of them, since that verse opens instead with the waw-plus-perfect וְשָׁכַ֥ן (byte tier). The claimed parallel is an artifact of one English word rendering two different Hebrew constructions, and it is the sole support offered for declining that cut. The row also quotes no Hebrew anywhere; its only oshb: refs are mark citations. Distinct limb B, second part, upheld with its supporting citation CORRECTED: the row names one internal imperative address at Isa.35.3, חַזְּק֖וּ יָדַ֣יִם רָפ֑וֹת (oshb:Isa.35.3, byte tier), and not the second -- oshb:Isa.35.4 opens אִמְרוּ֙ לְנִמְהֲרֵי לֵ֔ב (byte tier), a verse-initial imperative, so the row's account of its own internal texture is incomplete. That stands. But the challenge supports it by pointing to הִנֵּ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ in the same verse as the same particle class treated as an onset driver elsewhere in this stretch, and that citation is loose on two counts: the form there is a different lexeme from the presentative used at the two verse-initial sites in this stretch, and it stands mid-verse rather than verse-initial. The finding rests on the imperative, not on the presentative; strike the presentative from the reasoning. Credited and verified: apparatus disclosure is complete and correctly typed for the span -- the interior SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.35.2, the closing PE at oshb:Isa.35.10 and the front-seam SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.34.17, all matching the single-witness inventory with PE and SAMEKH never conflated, and no paseq and no variant note falls in chapter 35. The row stops at the frame seam without crossing it. HIGH severity: a two-band cap overshoot plus a verbatim-fidelity breach on the row's own boundary-closing citation.
boundary_proposals.remedy: Author wave, one pass, no boundary change proposed by either lens. (1) Delete the inserted U+0022 from the closing quotation so the quoted run ends on the source's own single U+201D. Verbatim fidelity is character-level, so re-cut the quote by splicing from source rather than by editing the existing string. (2) confidence: high to medium_low, a two-band drop, with the same low-band consequences as the other members of this class -- three-sidecar mirroring with full schemas and a frontier-queue row for this chunk, bespoke why_low_confidence text keyed to the whole-chapter extent. (3) strongest_rejected_alternative: strike the cross-part adverb parallel entirely. It is byte-false -- the two verses do not share a construction -- and it is the only support the field offers, so the rival must be re-declined on a ground that exists in the Hebrew, with the adverb spliced pointed, its two adjacent verse-initial sites named, and its 6-verse book-wide digit carried. (4) boundary_rationale or device_notes: name the second internal imperative onset at oshb:Isa.35.4 alongside the one already named, spliced pointed with its tier. Do NOT rest that disclosure on the presentative in the same verse -- it is a different lexeme from the verse-initial presentative used elsewhere in this stretch and it stands mid-verse. Add oshb:Isa.35.3, oshb:Isa.35.4, oshb:Isa.35.5 and oshb:Isa.35.6 to boundary_evidence_refs. Cure test -- the tests that killed the original: a character-level comparison of every quoted English run against source must return an exact match with no inserted characters; and no rejected-alternative ground may rest on two verses sharing an English word where the Hebrew constructions differ, checked by splicing both.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: OL: the join across the chapter division is byte-supportable, but the row never quotes the catchword that supports it, never engages the one tier-3 mark inside its span that falls exactly at the junction it joins, and leaves a byte-true covering-in-sackcloth tie straddling its own closing seam undisclosed. boundary_proposals.grounds: CONVERGENCE: the two challenges land on ONE defect at the row's FORWARD seam, reached from opposite directions, plus two items that belong to OL alone. SAME DEFECT (LF's whole challenge = OL's third item). Bytes: MT 36:22 closes with the delegation as subject, וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ ל֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.36.22, byte); MT 37:1 opens a fresh wayehi-plus-explicit-subject clause, וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ (oshb:Isa.37.1, byte), shifting the acting subject from the delegation to the king; its וַיִּתְכַּ֣ס בַּשָּׂ֔ק (oshb:Isa.37.1, byte) is picked up immediately at MT 37:2 by מִתְכַּסִּ֖ים בַּשַּׂקִּ֑ים (oshb:Isa.37.2, byte) - the same verbal root in a different stem plus the same noun pluralized, ROOT tier, not byte-identical - while MT 37:2 itself opens וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח (oshb:Isa.37.2, byte) with Hezekiah still the subject. One defect, one cure. DISTINCT, OL ONLY (a): the sole PE or SAMEKH inside MT 36:21-37:1 is the SAMEKH at MT 36:22 - keyed to the verse immediately before the row's own INTERNAL join. Tier-3 weak, single-witness, never a driver, and its absence would never be counterevidence; but PRESENCE exactly at the join the row makes turns the row's one disclosed corroborating signal into a weak rival to its own decision, disclosed without its bearing stated. DISTINCT, OL ONLY (b): the join's strongest byte warrant goes unquoted - קְרוּעֵ֣י בְגָדִ֑ים (oshb:Isa.36.22, byte) answered across the junction by וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת בְּגָדָ֑יו (oshb:Isa.37.1, byte): shared root, distinct pointed forms, ROOT tier and not byte-identical recurrence - while the row argues 'the same participants and the same report-and-response movement' in English. The challenge's tier label there is exact. SCOPE, stated so the author wave cannot over-reach: the respan LF's rival implies - carrying 37:1 forward with Hezekiah's response - is a BOUNDARY PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption, and is never author work. Every remedy below is prose and disclosure repair only and leaves the bound exactly as drafted.

SCOPE, by census over the frozen corpus: positional row references stand at 32 occurrences in 24 of 225 rows, and the bare artifact noun at 526 occurrences in 170 of 225 rows, with the validator suite green throughout. This is therefore a corpus-wide register class, not a c22 defect, and four separate medium findings against it in one cluster overstate it; severity drops to low. The packet's own application is uneven: the last row of this cluster uses the artifact noun twice in its device_notes and was supported without a register challenge. The underlying seam is sound and byte-confirmed, exactly as the challenge concedes: oshb:Isa.49.8 opens כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (byte), verse-initial and an inventoried divine frame, and the closing verse opens with a presentative, הִנֵּה אֵ֕לֶּה (oshb:Isa.49.12, byte); both of the row's splices are literal substrings of their cited verses at byte tier. (i) Replace the positional reference in P14-003.strongest_rejected_alternative with a verse-anchored content term; leave the two non-positional, verse-anchored clauses alone unless the owner pins a stricter convention, and run the change as ONE corpus-wide register pass over the 32 positional occurrences in 24 rows rather than as four c22 edits. A byte-true lexical chain straddling a row's own seam argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and the rival field does consider the merge but rests only on the voice contrast and never names the device, so the rival is disclosed while its actual evidence is not. The second limb also verifies: oshb:Isa.49.15 opens הֲתִשְׁכַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ עוּלָ֔הּ (byte), a third-person rhetorical question about a woman and the son of her womb, and its only second-person element is the closing suffix in אֶשְׁכָּחֵֽךְ, so 'opens a new second-person address' misdescribes what opens that verse. LF LIMB REFUTED: the clause cited, opening a fresh row at web:Isa.49.19, carries an explicit verse anchor and names no position, and the register rule bars positional row references while requiring cross-row references to be verse-anchored -- this clause satisfies both. The positional-reference census confirms it: this row carries ZERO positional row references, against one each in the three sibling rows filed identically in the same packet.

The preceding verse is Zion's own quoted words, וְאָמַ֣רְתְּ בִּלְבָבֵ֗ךְ (oshb:Isa.49.21, byte), and the seam turns from her reported speech back to divine speech about her; the correction re-describes the shift rather than deleting it. (ii) Fill device_notes with the cross-seam disclosure of the continuing feminine address across oshb:Isa.49.15-Isa.49.23, tokens present in every verse. (iii) Apply the corpus-wide register pass to the positional reference. Add oshb:Isa.49.21 to boundary_evidence_refs. What holds and must be preserved: the interrogative onset הֲיֻקַּ֥ח מִגִּבּ֖וֹר (oshb:Isa.49.24, byte) is byte-true and the SAMEKH marks at both edges are correctly typed and single-witness-disclosed.
