boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The unit's load-bearing structural warrant -- an infinitive purpose chain running unbroken to the unit's own close -- is not what the pointed bytes carry, and the finite-clause differentia used to place the seam at Isa.61.4 is already met one clause earlier, inside this span.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The finding is byte-true; the account of HOW the chain breaks is partly not, so this refines rather than upholds flat. UPHELD, and it is the load-bearing half: oshb:Isa.61.3 runs 24 tokens; token 17 is כֵּהָ֑ה carrying the verse's main caesura, and token 18 opens וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ (byte tier), a waw-plus-perfect finite clause; the row's own quoted closing word לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) is token 24, inside that finite clause. The row's warrant, that the purpose chain 'runs without a finite-verb break through the unit's own close', is therefore byte-false at the unit's own close. UPHELD with a correction: וּבָנוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) is the same waw-plus-perfect construction, so that construction is not unique to the seam verse -- but the row's stated differentia is a finite THIRD-PERSON-PLURAL clause, and the 61:3b verb is not third-person-plural, so the criterion is not identically satisfied inside the span; only its finite-clause half is. NOT UPHELD, the framing leg: מָשַׁח֩ and שְׁלָחַ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier) do not 'break' the chain twice. The row names the sending as the chain's GOVERNOR, and all six infinitives after it follow it; counting the governing perfects as breaks reads against the row's own claim rather than against it. UPHELD, the re-tiering leg, and it is the second real defect: לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.60.21) and לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3) are byte-identical (sweep: 2 verses book-wide for that form), while the planting nouns are not -- oshb:Isa.60.21 stages the ketiv/qere pair מטעו מַטָּעַ֛י (unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere, byte tier) against oshb:Isa.61.3's מַטַּ֥ע (sweep: 3 verses on that consonantal string, skeleton tier: oshb:Isa.14.19, oshb:Isa.60.21, oshb:Isa.61.3). The row's device_notes calls the pair a 'collocation' and a 'catchword' with NO tier label at all, which is precisely the tier-disclosure standard's failure mode, and the apparatus doubling at the earlier verse is not disclosed either. NEW FINDING (neither lens): the paseq inventory records 1 seg at MT 61:3, inside this row's own span, undisclosed, while sibling rows in these clusters do disclose their span-relevant paseq. The unconditional span-relevant symmetry sweep covers the parashah layer, not paseq, so this is a disclosure-consistency gap rather than a validator failure -- recorded at low weight. The anointed-speaker hold is untouched and stays open: no eved-root token stands in oshb:Isa.61.1-Isa.61.3 (sweep: 0 eved-root tokens over the unit's 3 verses), the challenge does not contest the hold, and this ruling does not decide it.
boundary_proposals.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace 'runs without a finite-verb break through the unit's own close' with a formulation that names the waw-plus-perfect opening oshb:Isa.61.3's second half after the caesura, and state the seam differentia as the SUBJECT change (the mourners named in the impersonal-passive clause at 61:3b against the third-person-plural community at 61:4), not as the presence or absence of a finite verb. device_notes: tier-label the catchword -- byte-identical only at the 'to be glorified' form, the planting nouns skeleton-level and ketiv/qere-doubled at oshb:Isa.60.21 -- quoting each spliced form; and add the span-interior paseq disclosure at MT 61:3 (count-only, single-witness, no position asserted). boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: LF: this unit's own opening simile reuses, at the accent-stripped tier, the garland word that closes the anointed speaker's commission three verses earlier -- an undisclosed recurrence bearing on the very speaker question the row leaves open. OL: two undisclosed lexical hooks in the opening verse reach back across the front seam into both preceding units, and the close rests on the chapter division plus a genre contrast rather than on anything the bytes mark.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The two items share ONE core defect and each adds one distinct leg. SAME DEFECT, upheld: the garland non-disclosure. פְּאֵ֜ר (oshb:Isa.61.3, token 6, byte tier) against פְּאֵ֔ר (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) differ only in cantillation and are identical at accent_stripped tier; the standalone token stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, oshb:Isa.61.3 and oshb:Isa.61.10). Both lenses tier it correctly and the row discloses it nowhere. Under the cross-seam cohesion rule a byte-true device reaching across the row's own front seam argues continuity unless disclosed, and here it is not neutral texture: the row's device_notes leaves open whether the rejoicing voice is 'the same figure who speaks beginning at Isa.61.1', which is exactly what the garland tie bears on. OL's asymmetry point is also correct and aggravating -- the unit opening at 61:1 disclosed the catchword at its OWN edge while this one discloses none. DISTINCT leg (OL), REFINED inside this uphold: the priest-root hook is a real ROOT echo -- כֹּהֲנֵ֤י (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier) against יְכַהֵ֣ן (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) -- but OL's framing and digit are defective. The two tokens do not carry 'the same consonants'; only the three-letter root is shared. Swept per attested spelling, the 61:10 verb form stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier) and the 61:6 noun form in 4 (sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier: oshb:Isa.10.15, oshb:Isa.37.2, oshb:Isa.61.6, oshb:Isa.66.21) -- and that 4 blends the priest noun with a preposition-plus-verb string at oshb:Isa.10.15, a contiguous-substring false hit of exactly the class the hazard catalogue names. So 'sweep: 4 verses for each attested spelling' is wrong for one spelling and count-object-blended for the other; the leg survives only as a root echo across a two-verse gap and carries far less weight than the garland tie. DISTINCT leg (OL), upheld: the back seam. The row's closing sentence ends 'closing this unit at the chapter division', and chapter divisions are tier-4, never boundary evidence. The residual rhetorical-mode contrast is real, but the first-person-singular voice runs straight across the seam -- שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) against לֹ֣א אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה and לֹ֣א אֶשְׁק֑וֹט (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier) -- and that continuity is undisclosed. NEW FINDING (neither lens): 1 paseq seg stands at MT 61:11, inside this row's own span, undisclosed -- the same disclosure-consistency class recorded on P17-002 at MT 61:3, and again not a validator failure. The speaker's identity stays open; this ruling does not decide it.
boundary_proposals.remedy: device_notes: add the garland disclosure -- splice the noun from oshb:Isa.61.3 and oshb:Isa.61.10, name the tier as accent_stripped (byte differs by cantillation), name the swept object (standalone token, 2 verses book-wide), and state explicitly that the tie is disclosed continuity that does NOT resolve the held speaker question; add the span-interior paseq at MT 61:11 (count-only, single-witness). boundary_rationale: delete 'at the chapter division' and re-ground the back seam on the rhetorical-mode contrast alone, disclosing that the first-person-singular voice runs across the seam into oshb:Isa.62.1. If the priest-root echo is carried at all, carry it as a ROOT echo with per-spelling digits (verb form 1 verse; noun form 4 verses, one of them a substring false hit) and never as 'the same consonants'. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: re-run the cross-seam cohesion read over oshb:Isa.61.3-Isa.62.1 and confirm no byte-true or accent-true device straddling either of this row's edges is left unnamed, and that every digit written names its swept object. boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The seam is carried by an 'explicit vocative' and a 'new first-person divine act' at Isa.62.6 that the bytes do not supply, while the second-feminine-singular addressee runs straight through it.
boundary_proposals.grounds: UPHELD on all three legs, with one qualification on the first. Leg 1: oshb:Isa.62.6 opens עַל חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם (byte tier) -- the city name stands in apposition with no vocative particle or marker. QUALIFICATION: Hebrew vocatives are ordinarily unmarked, so the defect is not that an address is impossible but that the row calls it EXPLICIT and treats the naming of the addressee as a CHANGE of addressee. Leg 2, and this is the load-bearing one: the addressee is continuous across the claimed seam. This unit's own last two words are עָלַ֖יִךְ אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ (oshb:Isa.62.5, byte tier, 2fs) and the first suffixed word of the next verse is the 2fs form in עַל חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם -- the same addressee either side. OL's suffix census re-derives correctly at accent-stripped tier (oshb:Isa.62.2 three tokens, 62:3 one, 62:4 six, 62:5 four, 62:6 one, 62:7 none, 62:8 three), and the address carries on past the following seam at דְּגָנֵ֨ךְ, לְאֹ֣יְבַ֔יִךְ and תִּֽירוֹשֵׁ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.8, byte tier). So the row's stated ground -- an opening 'that this unit's own address to Zion does not share' -- is byte-contradicted. Leg 3: 'new first-person divine act' fails on both qualifiers. oshb:Isa.62.1 already carries לֹ֣א אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה and לֹ֣א אֶשְׁק֑וֹט (byte tier), so the person is not new. On the 'divine' half the challenge is right but its wording is byte-false and needs correcting -- and the corrected form is stronger for it. The divine name is NOT absent from Isa.62.1-Isa.62.6: it stands in 4 of those 6 verses (sweep: 4 verses carrying the tetragrammaton over the 6-verse stretch -- oshb:Isa.62.2, oshb:Isa.62.3, oshb:Isa.62.4, oshb:Isa.62.6 -- beside the suffixed 'your God' at oshb:Isa.62.3 and oshb:Isa.62.5). What is true, and decisive, is that EVERY one of those occurrences is THIRD person relative to the first-person voice, including inside the seam verse itself, where the addressed group is told to remind הַמַּזְכִּרִים֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier). So the first-person speaker is nowhere identified with the named deity, and the divine attribution at the seam verse is inference -- the unnamed-speaker class a chunking row should hold rather than drive a seam with. NEW FINDING (neither lens): the row's own front-portion sentence, that 'the same second-person address to Zion runs through the renaming and marriage imagery', starts one verse late. oshb:Isa.62.1 carries no second-person token at all; Zion is referred to in the third person there -- צִדְקָ֔הּ וִישׁוּעָתָ֖הּ (byte tier, 3fs suffixes). The 2fs address begins at oshb:Isa.62.2. This is an independent defect in the row's own internal description and it strengthens the continuity finding. CONFIDENCE: the row records high. With both named differentiae byte-contested and the residual seam signal reduced to the introduction of a participant group inside a continuous addressee and a continuous voice, high is not carried by the bytes. Not challenged and confirmed: the ketiv/qere handling at oshb:Isa.62.3 stages both forms side by side, and the parashah-absence statement is inventory-correct (segs stand at MT 61:9 and MT 62:9, none between).
boundary_proposals.remedy: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: strike 'an explicit vocative' and 'a new first-person divine act' as the seam's differentiae; re-ground the seam on what the bytes do carry -- the introduction of a new participant group (posted watchmen) and the shift of the speaker's own act from vow to appointment -- and ADD the disclosure that both the 2fs addressee and the 1cs voice run across the seam. Correct the front-portion sentence: the second-person address begins at oshb:Isa.62.2, not at the unit's opening verse, which speaks of Zion in the third person. confidence: lower from high (a row-field change, not a respan), and mirror the row into the sidecars with a bespoke why_low_confidence naming the unmarked-seam problem. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: re-run the addressee-suffix read over oshb:Isa.62.1-Isa.62.8 and confirm no field states a differentia that is satisfied on BOTH sides of this row's own seam. No span change proposed.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: The cohesion argument and the rejected alternative both attribute the 'give no rest' summons to the watchmen, but in the bytes that summons is addressed to them by the same speaker who posted them.
boundary_proposals.grounds: UPHELD, byte-confirmed and load-bearing. The second half of oshb:Isa.62.6 reads אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם and oshb:Isa.62.7 opens וְאַֽל תִּתְּנ֥וּ (both byte tier): both are addressed second-person-plural forms, and the English witness reads the same way. No petition is uttered BY the watchmen anywhere in Isa.62.6-Isa.62.9; the commands are laid ON them by the speaker who posted them. The row's 'The watchmen's own summons' and its rejected alternative's 'the watchmen's own petition' therefore name a speech role the bytes do not attest -- a speech-role misassignment of exactly the class the campaign's role-split discipline exists to catch. The defect is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: the ONLY stated ground for not splitting at the oath verse is that 'the sworn content answers the watchmen's own petition'. Remove the petition and the rejected alternative is left undefeated, so the row's rival disclosure is empty as written. OL's second leg is upheld and is the sharper half: the addressee alternates inside the span -- 2fs in עַל חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם (oshb:Isa.62.6), 2mp at אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם and וְאַֽל תִּתְּנ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.62.6-Isa.62.7), 2fs again at דְּגָנֵ֨ךְ and תִּֽירוֹשֵׁ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.8), all byte tier -- and it is undisclosed in a row whose FRONT-seam argument turns on an addressee shift. That asymmetry, not the label alone, is what makes the item medium. NEW FINDING (neither lens): the same misattribution PROPAGATES. P17-007's boundary_rationale and its strongest_rejected_alternative both re-use 'the watchmen's own petition' / 'the watchmen's own intercession', so the corrected speech role must be swept across both rows in one edit rather than spot-fixed here. Not challenged and confirmed: נִשְׁבַּ֧ע יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.62.8, byte tier) does open the oath-negative construction running to the unit's close, and the setumah at MT 62:9 is inventory-true, correctly typed, single-witness, and the only span-relevant parashah seg (sweep: 1 parashah seg over the span's 4 Masoretic verses).
boundary_proposals.remedy: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cast the speech role -- the imperatives at MT 62:6b-62:7 are addressed TO the posted watchmen by the speaker, not uttered by them. Restate the cohesion argument as the oath answering the charge the speaker lays on the watchmen, and give the rejected split at the oath verse a ground that survives that correction. device_notes: disclose the 2fs / 2mp / 2fs addressee alternation inside the span with spliced tokens and tier, since an addressee shift is the row's own front-seam driver. Apply the identical speech-role correction to P17-007's two fields in the SAME edit -- seam-pair cures are one edit and symmetry completion is a sweep, not a spot fix. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: re-read oshb:Isa.62.6-Isa.62.7 and confirm no field in either row attributes a petition, summons or intercession to the watchmen as SPEAKERS, and that the rejected alternative still has a ground once the misattribution is gone. No span change.

boundary_proposals.challenge_claim: LF: the closing rationale leans on an unnamed chapter-spanning renaming bracket without citing the recurring form that carries it, and never weighs the rival that the same bracket argues for one larger bracketed unit across the chapter. OL: both edges are genuinely corroborated, but the stated onset differentia does not discriminate -- the group commanded at Isa.62.10 is the group already commanded in the preceding verses -- and the bracketing claim is under-specified.
boundary_proposals.grounds: The two items overlap on one leg and diverge on two; the shared leg is upheld but needs re-anchoring, so this refines. SHARED and upheld: the bracket is asserted without naming the form. The recurring form is real -- יִקָּרֵא֙ (oshb:Isa.62.4, byte tier) and יִקָּרֵ֣א (oshb:Isa.62.12, byte tier), identical at accent_stripped tier and differing only in cantillation -- and the row names neither. LF's tiering is right, including its honest note that עֲזוּבָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.62.4) against נֶעֱזָֽבָה (oshb:Isa.62.12) is a root-level echo only, the two forms standing in different stems. REFINED, and this is the corrected finding: OL's anchor is the better one. The row says the renaming pair 'brackets the resolve opened at Isa.62.1', but that verse carries no renaming at all. What the closing renaming answers is וְקֹ֤רָא לָךְ֙ שֵׁ֣ם חָדָ֔שׁ (oshb:Isa.62.2, byte tier) together with the renaming at oshb:Isa.62.4. So the bracket is not merely unnamed -- it is mis-anchored by one verse onto a verse that carries no member of the pair. LF's 'unnamed' framing understates this and OL's 'under-specified' understates it in the other direction. ordinary_cures.challenge_claim: The row leans on a ketiv/qere-bearing verse for its internal mark disclosure without any apparatus disclosure, and rests its closing device on a divine title whose Hebrew object it never names - one the English rendering flattens into the same words as the different stack quoted at the neighbouring seam.
ordinary_cures.grounds: Byte-re-derived; both prongs are real but both need reframing, so refine. PRONG 1 (ketiv/qere): the site is real — MT 10:32 carries one note, staged as the doubled pair inside הַ֣ר בית בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן (web:Isa.10.32, byte tier for the spliced run; the ketiv member is unpointed and is skeleton grade standing alone) — and this row is the strongest of the five such cases in these clusters, because it does not merely contain the verse: it lists web:Isa.10.32 in its own evidence refs and argues from that verse's paragraph mark, engaging the verse while passing over its apparatus. CORPUS EVIDENCE I DERIVED FOR THIS RULING (and which corrects my own earlier framing of this class): across the whole frozen corpus, 43 rows have a ketiv/qere verse inside their span; 35 of them disclose it and 8 do not. Five of those eight sit in these two clusters, and this writer part discloses in only 1 of its 5 such rows, while a sibling part carries the attested formulation for exactly this case — a reference entry reading 'ketiv/qere note, single-witness; content not sliced'. So disclosure of an in-span ketiv/qere verse is settled corpus PRACTICE at a 35-of-43 rate, not merely one part's habit. It is still NOT a Tier-0 debt: the mark-check's unconditional span-relevant symmetry sweep covers petuchah and setumah only, its ketiv/qere arm validates claims that are made, and this row passes every Tier-0 check clean. The primaries reach the right conclusion by the wrong rationale — nothing is 'owed before slicing', because no slicing occurs; what is real is a documented practice deviation. PRONG 2 (divine title): the byte facts verify but the framing overstates. The row does not rest its closing device on a title — its device is the presentative formula, and it splices the Hebrew הִנֵּ֤ה הָאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.33, byte tier) at byte tier, rendered “Behold, the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, will lop the boughs with terror. The in-chapter recurrence at הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.16, byte tier) is identical to the closing stack at accent-stripped and skeleton tier but NOT at byte tier, and it sits two rows away rather than across this row's own seam, so the cross-seam cohesion rule does not trigger — it is a recurrence to name, not a straddling device. ordinary_cures.challenge_claim: The cut itself is well founded on the bytes, but both structural claims the row offers as its grounds - the stump image answering the felled trees across its front seam, and the closing inclusio - are asserted with no quoted Hebrew form and no tier label, and neither has a byte-level anchor.

The cut itself is sound and not contested: the onset splice וְיָצָ֥א חֹ֖טֶר מִגֵּ֣זַע יִשָׁ֑י (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier) matches the source bytes and enters a fresh grammatical subject, “A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.” (web:Isa.11.1); the mark layer is right (setumah at MT 10:34, petuchah at MT 11:9, correct types, none inside MT 11:1-11:8, and no ketiv/qere note anywhere in the span, so nothing is owed there). ONE FRAMING NOTE, not adopted and not needed for the defect: the challenge's evidence adds that a semantic continuity across the row's own seam argues against the cut rather than for it. That inference is available but optional — the row can equally be read as disclosing a cross-seam echo, which is the right register; the defect stands either way, because on either reading the claim carries no form and no tier. The back seam is sounder and the challenge says so: the figure does continue into the next verse, מִשָּׁרָשָׁ֥יו (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier) answered by שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ יִשַׁ֗י (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier). ordinary_cures.grounds: Both primaries hit this row; most items verify, one OL support is REFUTED on the bytes and one LF scope claim needs narrowing, so refine. The book carries exactly three headers of this class (MT 1:1, 2:1, 13:1), so setting this one apart would make a THIRD such row, not a fourth; the sentence names two precedents and then miscounts its own addition. OL's proposed discriminator checks out on the bytes: this header binds its target to the burden-noun in construct, מַשָּׂ֖א בָּבֶ֑ל (oshb:Isa.13.1, byte tier), while the other attaches its target with a preposition after the patronymic, בֶּן אָמ֑וֹץ עַל יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Isa.2.1, byte tier). I also checked OL's digit against its object and it is RIGHT where it could easily have been wrong: the verb-then-prophet adjacency stands at exactly 2 verses (MT 2:1 and 13:1), because MT 1:1 places the name BEFORE the verb — a different object from the 3-verse relative clause. OL ITEM 2, REFUTED AS STATED: the ketiv/qere site at MT 13:16 is real, staged as the doubled pair וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם תשגלנה תִּשָּׁכַֽבְנָה (oshb:Isa.13.16, byte tier for the spliced run), and this row is one of the 8 undisclosed cases corpus-wide against 35 disclosed. The site survives as a practice deviation; the reason given for it does not. VERIFIES: the header is verse-initial and correctly kept with its oracle; petuchah at MT 12:6 correct type; no petuchah or setumah inside MT 13:1-13:16 (absence never counterevidence); one paseq at MT 13:8, single-witness, count-only.
ordinary_cures.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). ordinary_cures.challenge_claim: The mandated rival is described in terms the cited verse's bytes contradict - as worded it restates the row's own bound rather than an alternative - and the rear-edge frame claim carries no quoted frame form.
ordinary_cures.grounds: All four items confirmed from bytes, and a fifth defect neither primary raised is recorded below. (1) UPHELD. The rival proposes 'extending this unit through Isaiah's own questioning at web:Isa.39.5'. MT 39:5 carries no interrogative whatever: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ שְׁמַ֖ע דְּבַר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Isa.39.5, byte) - a summons, whose three-token frame שְׁמַ֖ע דְּבַר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת is the SOLE site of that formula in the book (sweep: 1 verse, byte and finals-normalized skeleton alike). The prophet's questioning stands at MT 39:3, מָ֥ה אָמְר֣וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה וּמֵאַ֨יִן֙ יָבֹ֣אוּ, and at MT 39:4, וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מָ֥ה רָא֖וּ בְּבֵיתֶ֑ךָ (byte tier) - both INSIDE this row's own span. So as worded the rival names the row's existing bound rather than an alternative to it, and the same sentence then attributes a herald-summons to that same verse, contradicting its own label. Read charitably the INTENT is a genuine rival - a cut after MT 39:5 rather than after MT 39:4 - which is why the cure is a re-wording and not the invention of a new rival; but this is the mandated rival field, and a field whose two halves label one verse incompatibly cannot stand. (2) UPHELD. The rear-edge warrant is a frame-based seam claim - the following unit is 'introduced by a fresh herald-summons' - with no frame form quoted anywhere in the row. The form exists, is short, and is unique in the book, so the omission is not a shortage of evidence. (3) UPHELD, minor. The ketiv/qere at MT 39:2 is correctly disclosed against the inventory's single note there, but the row does not name which of the two staged forms its treasury gloss follows; the pair stands as נכתה נְכֹת֡וֹ in the verse bytes (oshb:Isa.39.2, byte), the first form unpointed. A row that slices a K/Q verse names the forms. (4) UPHELD. The oracle takes Hezekiah's own wording back up across the row's rear edge: כָּל אֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּבֵיתִי֙ at MT 39:4 against כָּל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵיתֶ֗ךָ at MT 39:6 (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, finals-normalized skeleton tier), with the treasury chain running MT 39:2 בְּאֹֽצְרֹתָ֑יו - DEFECTIVE - MT 39:4 בְּאוֹצְרֹתָֽי - PLENE - and MT 39:6 אָצְר֧וּ (byte tier). A plene/defective pair two verses apart inside one chain is the mater-lectionis hazard class in miniature; note for the author that a raw consonantal sweep of that root BLENDS a second root and must not be cited as a treasury digit - name the three attested sites instead. NEW FINDING (raised by neither primary): device_notes asserts that 'the embassy's own display-of-treasury motif closes without remainder before Isaiah's separate judgment word begins.' That is an AFFIRMATIVE claim the bytes contradict, not merely an undisclosed link: the motif demonstrably does NOT close without remainder, since both the possession-catchword and the treasury root are reactivated at MT 39:6, one verse into the following unit. ORDINAL: the messenger formula stands in exactly 5 verses inside MT 44:23-45:25 -- כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ at MT 44:24, כֹּה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ לִמְשִׁיחוֹ֮ לְכ֣וֹרֶשׁ at MT 45:1, כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְיֹצְר֑וֹ at MT 45:11, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה at MT 45:14 and כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר יְ֠הוָה at MT 45:18 (byte tier at each ref; sweep: 48 verses book-wide carry the formula) -- so MT 45:14 is the FOURTH onset, and the row reaches 'third' only by skipping the MT 45:11 frame that the neighbouring row itself treats as fresh. OL's added half is the sharper statement of the rule: the ordinal names no counted domain, and the domain cannot be inferred, because a ch-45-only count WOULD yield third while the sibling row numbers MT 45:1 'second' on a count that includes MT 44:24 -- semantic-class count discipline requires the object and the range be named before the digit. ADDRESSEE: byte-contradicted. Every addressee form in MT 45:14 is feminine singular -- עָלַ֤יִךְ יַעֲבֹ֨רוּ֙ וְלָ֣ךְ יִֽהְי֔וּ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.14) -- and the confession itself reads אַ֣ךְ בָּ֥ךְ אֵ֛ל (byte tier, same ref), the preposition carrying a final kaf with NO mappiq, i.e. feminine singular; MT 45:15 then opens אָכֵ֕ן אַתָּ֖ה אֵ֣ל מִסְתַּתֵּ֑ר (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.15) with a masculine singular independent pronoun. The shift is byte-visible whichever speaker is assigned to the confession, since the addressee changes from the city to the deity inside the reported speech itself. The row may still keep MT 45:15 inside the confession, but it must argue that from the reported-speech frame: arguing from the absence of a tier-1 signal is legitimate only when the absence is real, and here it is not. Credit, so the author does not disturb it: the paseq disclosure is exemplary -- count-only, single-witness, position expressly not claimed -- and MT 45:14 is verified as the ONLY paseq-bearing verse in MT 44:23-45:25; the parashah disclosure is symmetric and correctly typed (PE after MT 45:13 before the span, PE after MT 45:17 at its close, tier-3, single-witness). Severity is OL's medium rather than LF's low: the ordinal alone would be low, but the byte-false absence is the stated ground of the row's own internal decision.
ordinary_cures.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-015. (a) Field device_notes: replace the clause grounding the decision on no addressee shift at MT 45:15 with the byte-true argument -- the addressee turns from feminine singular at MT 45:14, עָלַ֤יִךְ יַעֲבֹ֨רוּ֙ וְלָ֣ךְ יִֽהְי֔וּ and אַ֣ךְ בָּ֥ךְ אֵ֛ל, to masculine singular at MT 45:15, אָכֵ֕ן אַתָּ֖ה אֵ֣ל מִסְתַּתֵּ֑ר, each spliced at byte tier at its own ref, and MT 45:15 is nonetheless held inside the unit as the CONTINUATION OF THE REPORTED CONFESSION, which is the reported-speech frame doing the work; the honest absence to cite there is that no fresh messenger frame opens at MT 45:15. (b) Field boundary_rationale: either name the ordinal's counted object and range explicitly (messenger-formula onsets within MT 44:23-45:25, MT 45:14 being the fourth of five) or drop the ordinal and call it a fresh frame. The same edit is owed in the sibling row that numbers MT 45:18, so run it as ONE series-wide sweep across the part, not as separate spot fixes. Test the cure must pass: any ordinal in row prose names its counted object and range and re-derives against a sweep of that range -- the test that killed the original was the five-onset count in MT 44:23-45:25 -- and any claim that a signal is absent re-checks against the pointed bytes on both sides of the seam it argues.

ordinary_cures.challenge_claim: LF (low): the row's label of Isa.45.18 as the 'fourth koh-amar frame' undercounts the same sequence -- by the five-onset count it is the fifth, the undercount again omitting Isa.45.11. OL (medium): the addressee contrast offered as this row's seam driver is half absent from the bytes -- Isa.45.18-Isa.45.19 carry no vocative and no second-person addressee at all, so there is no 'address to the offspring of Jacob' for 45:20's summons to shift away from -- plus the same unnamed-enumeration ordinal.
ordinary_cures.grounds: CONVERGENCE: the ordinal is the SAME defect in both packets AND the same series defect already ruled on the sibling row -- one cure, not three. The addressee-contrast item is DISTINCT to OL and is the substantive finding here. Both verify. ORDINAL: by the verified five-onset count inside MT 44:23-45:25, MT 45:18 is the FIFTH, not the fourth; the series skips the MT 45:11 frame exactly as at the sibling row, and no counted domain is named. ADDRESSEE CONTRAST: byte-exact and the more serious. MT 45:18 is third- and first-person throughout -- its object suffixes are all feminine singular referring to the earth, לֹא תֹ֥הוּ בְרָאָ֖הּ לָשֶׁ֣בֶת יְצָרָ֑הּ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.18), closing on a first-person self-declaration -- and MT 45:19 is first-person report whose only mention of Jacob's offspring is לֹ֥א אָמַ֛רְתִּי לְזֶ֥רַע יַעֲקֹ֖ב תֹּ֣הוּ בַקְּשׁ֑וּנִי (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.19), where the offspring stand as the indirect object of a NEGATED report and the plural imperative inside it sits within the quoted speech being denied. There is no vocative and no second-person verb or suffix anywhere in the row's span, so the row's device_notes sets MT 45:20's onset against an address that does not exist in its own span. The seam itself is not in doubt and I do not disturb it: MT 45:20 opens הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וָבֹ֛אוּ הִֽתְנַגְּשׁ֥וּ יַחְדָּ֖ו פְּלִיטֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֑ם (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.20) -- three plural imperative forms followed by the addressed group -- which is sufficient tier-1 evidence standing alone. One precision on the challenge's wording: Hebrew marks no vocative, so 'plural vocative' is a construal resting on the three plural imperatives rather than a byte-marked form; the imperatives are the byte-visible part and should carry the claim. The rival is correctly credited: the exclusive-deity formula does straddle the seam, וְאֵ֥ין עֽוֹד at MT 45:18 (byte tier) recurring at MT 45:21 and MT 45:22 (sweep: 7 verses book-wide carry that skeleton, 6 of them in ch 45), and the row discloses the joined-speech reading. The frame's non-initial position is handled honestly -- the row splices the causal particle with the formula, כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר יְ֠הוָה (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.18), with the tetragrammaton immediately following, so the frame owner is the divine class. Marks: PE after MT 45:17 before the span, none inside (tier-3, single-witness).
ordinary_cures.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-016. (b) Field boundary_rationale: fix the ordinal in the SAME series-wide sweep as the sibling row -- name the counted object and range (messenger-formula onsets in MT 44:23-45:25, MT 45:18 being the fifth of five) or drop the ordinal. ordinary_cures.challenge_claim: The row's one recurrence claim -- that the summons takes up 'the same declare-and-witness vocabulary as the earlier trial speeches' -- carries no tier label, no digit, and no verse anchor, and the closing sentence grounds the row's rear edge in the work assignment rather than in the text.
ordinary_cures.grounds: Both defects verify and neither touches the bounds. (1) The recurrence claim names no verse, labels no tier and carries no digit, so it is evidence-free prose in a campaign where every recurrence is tier-labelled at write time and where no verse it argues can be mirrored in the evidence refs. The claim is checkable and true: the imperative pair is הַגִּ֣ידוּ וְהַגִּ֔ישׁוּ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.21), and that imperative's skeleton stands in 6 verses book-wide, the trial-speech sites among them being MT 41:22 and MT 41:23 (verified) -- so the fix is purely additive, which is why low is the right band. (2) The closing phrase 'the end of the assigned range' argues the row's rear edge from the work unit rather than from the text, which the register law bars outright: work-unit and file-order talk never appears in row prose, and cross-row references are verse-anchored. The honest byte statement is available -- MT 46:1 opens a different subject with a burden-noun, נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם עֲמוּס֔וֹת מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה (byte tier, oshb:Isa.46.1), which belongs to the load-carry family and not to the verse-initial oracle headers, so the following verse begins no header-bounded oracle. Bounds stand and I do not disturb them: MT 45:20's plural imperatives plus named addressed group are tier-1 and byte-verified, and the closing verdict is בַּיהוָ֛ה יִצְדְּק֥וּ וְיִֽתְהַלְל֖וּ כָּל זֶ֥רַע יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (byte tier, oshb:Isa.45.25). The mark report verifies exactly: no PE and no SAMEKH from MT 45:18 through MT 45:25, the layer's section running from the PE after MT 45:17 to the SAMEKH after MT 46:2. The challenge is right to present that grouping as running toward the row's disclosed rival AND right not to press it as a defect -- absence is never counterevidence and no mark stands adjacent to either seam -- so it stays out of the mandatory remedy. NEW FINDING, neither primary's: the row's own absence statement, that no marked-division disclosure applies within the span or at its front seam, is byte-checkable but carries no digit where the sanctioned shorthand would give one (0 marked verses in MT 45:20-45:25); a zero-count claim carries the same digit discipline as a positive one.
ordinary_cures.remedy: Work order for the author wave, P12-017. Test the cure must pass: no work-unit, file-order or positional reference survives anywhere in row prose, every recurrence carries verse anchors, tier and digit, and every verse newly argued in prose appears in the evidence refs -- the tests that killed the original were an unanchored recurrence claim and a rear edge grounded in the work assignment.

ordinary_cures.challenge_claim: Onset bytes and mark handling are sound, but the named three-part summons series is a blended, untiered object, the parenthetical that the first and third members repeat one shape is untiered and false at byte tier, and the row's own closing verse carries half of a byte-tier pair reaching to web:Isa.51.11 that no row in the chain discloses.
ordinary_cures.grounds: Two sub-claims upheld, one refined. (a) Blended, undigited series object -- UPHELD (byte + accent_stripped): the device note names a three-part summons series joining שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י (oshb:Isa.51.1, byte) and שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.51.7, byte) with הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.51.4, byte) under one label, with no tier and no digit. The summons opener itself stands at 4 verses book-wide from accent_stripped tier down (sweep: 4 verses -- oshb:Isa.46.3, oshb:Isa.46.12, oshb:Isa.51.1, oshb:Isa.51.7), two of them outside the claimed series, while the second member's opener is unique at every tier (sweep: 1 verse at byte, accent_stripped and skeleton). Naming the class without naming what was swept or at what tier is the count-discipline defect. (b) The parenthetical -- REFINED: 'the first and third repeating one shape' is untiered, and OL's 'false at byte tier' overstates what the wording asserts. The bytes: the imperative at oshb:Isa.51.1 carries U+05A5 and at oshb:Isa.51.7 carries U+05A4; collation of either opener against the other verse reaches accent_stripped tier and no further; the row's two-token opener is byte-unique (sweep: 1 verse, byte) while the third member's is byte-shared with oshb:Isa.46.3 (sweep: 2 verses, byte). Read as a form-class statement the parenthetical is true from accent_stripped down; read as identity it is false. The real defect is that it ships with no tier inside a field whose other Hebrew claims carry explicit tier labels. (c) Undisclosed recurrence on the row's own closing verse -- UPHELD (byte): this span closes on שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ (oshb:Isa.51.3, byte), which recurs byte-identically at oshb:Isa.51.11 and oshb:Isa.35.10 (sweep: 3 verses book-wide at byte tier; 4 at accent_stripped and skeleton, adding oshb:Isa.22.13). Two of the three byte sites are the closing verses of this span and of web:Isa.51.9-Isa.51.11, bracketing 51:3-51:11 across two intervening rows. It does not straddle this row's own seam, so it argues the larger complex rather than against this cut -- but it is a byte-true recurrence on the row's own closing verse and disclosure is owed. Confirmed sound and not disturbed: SAMEKH keyed to oshb:Isa.51.2 is disclosed as interior even though it cuts against the span, and PE at oshb:Isa.50.11 and SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.3 are typed and single-witness-labelled; no ketiv/qere note and no paseq seg falls anywhere in ch 51, so nothing further is owed on those layers.
ordinary_cures.remedy: Author wave, row P14-011. (a) device_notes: name the swept object before the series label and carry a digit and a tier -- the summons opener at 4 verses book-wide from accent_stripped down, the second member's opener unique at every tier -- or drop the collective label. (b) strongest_rejected_alternative: give the 'one shape' parenthetical its tier (accent_stripped) or delete it. ordinary_cures.challenge_claim: Two load-bearing byte claims in the boundary rationale are false: the preceding span's closing verse carries no moth-and-worm imagery, and the two summons openers do not match at byte tier.
ordinary_cures.grounds: Re-derived from the bytes; the first claim is a hard error and it is load-bearing. (b) UPHELD, framing tightened (byte / accent_stripped): the rationale's 'returning to' and the device note's 'matches the series' first member's shape' are recurrence claims carrying no tier of their own, sitting immediately beside a byte-tier label that belongs to the splice at its own verse. In the bytes שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ at oshb:Isa.51.7 and שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י at oshb:Isa.51.1 differ (U+05A4 against U+05A5) and agree only from accent_stripped tier down; the byte-tier partner of this row's two-token opener lies outside the claimed series entirely (sweep: 2 verses at byte -- oshb:Isa.46.3, oshb:Isa.51.7). (b) Add the moth-and-garment link back to oshb:Isa.50.9 at its honest tier (word-bound skeleton, different token order; no shared two-token run at byte). ordinary_cures.challenge_claim: The span's unit label rests entirely on the one verse the row never engages in the bytes, the English run standing in for that verse is not the translation's wording, and calling that verse both the structural center and a match to a recognized hymn-closure pattern is self-contradictory and unevidenced.
ordinary_cures.grounds: All three sub-claims verified; one piece of OL's own supporting evidence is refuted. (a) UPHELD (byte): the doxological label is carried by the sung imperatives at oshb:Isa.52.9 -- פִּצְח֤וּ רַנְּנוּ֙ -- and that two-token run is unique book-wide at every tier (sweep: 1 verse at byte, accent_stripped and skeleton). oshb:Isa.52.9 is the only verse of this span with no pointed splice anywhere in the row; the three that are spliced (oshb:Isa.52.7, oshb:Isa.52.8, oshb:Isa.52.10) are exclamation, report and announcement, not sung imperative. The label's actual byte warrant therefore goes unstated while an unquoted verse carries it. NEW FINDING sharpening this: that verse appears in NO evidence ref, either witness, although device_notes argues from it -- while every other verse the row argues is listed under both witnesses. This is an internal asymmetry rather than a mirror-rule failure, since the verse lies inside the row's own span, but it is the same omission showing twice. (b) UPHELD (translation bytes): the device note's English run is set in straight quotes and is not the translation's wording -- the source reads “Break out into joy! Sing together, you waste places of Jerusalem;” (web:Isa.52.9), with an exclamation point and initial capitals where the row has a comma and lower case. Straight quoting keeps a non-verbatim run of translation text out of reach of the verbatim arm inside a field that carries that verse's own web: ref.
